schema.description: Details of the instance types that you specify by using the Extended Configurations feature of the launch template.

items.description: Launch template information.

InstanceType.description:
Instance type N that you want to use to override the instance type that is specified in the launch template. If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of the instances, you must specify the **LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType** and **LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity** parameters.

You can specify N instance types by using the Extended Configurations feature of the launch template. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  This parameter is available only if you specify the **LaunchTemplateId **parameter.

For information about the valid values of **InstanceType **in **InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType**, see the [Overview of instance families](~~25378~~) topic.

WeightedCapacity.description:
The weight of instance type N. The weight of an instance type specifies the capacity of an instance of the instance type in the scaling group. If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of the instances, you must specify the **LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity** parameter after you specify the **LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType** parameter. The values of N in the two parameters must be the same.

A higher weight specifies that a smaller number of instances of the specified instance type are required to meet the expected capacity requirement.

Performance metrics, such as the number of vCPUs and the memory size of each instance type, may vary. You can specify different weights for different instance types based on your business requirements.

Example:

*   Current capacity: 0
*   Expected capacity: 6
*   Capacity of ecs.c5.xlarge: 4

To meet the expected capacity requirement, Auto Scaling must create two ecs.c5.xlarge instances.

>  The capacity of the scaling group during a scale-out cannot exceed the sum of the maximum number of instances that is specified by the **MaxSize **parameter and the maximum weight of the instance types.

Valid values of **WeightedCapacity **in the **InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity** parameter: 1 to 500.

SpotPriceLimit.description:
The maximum bid price of instance type N that is specified by the `LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType` parameter. You can specify N instance types by using the Extended Configurations feature of the launch template. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  This parameter is available only if you specify the `LaunchTemplateId` parameter.

N specifies the serial number of the ALB server group. You can associate only a limited number of ALB server groups with a scaling group. Go to [Quota Center](https://quotas.console.aliyun.com/products/ess/quotas) to check the maximum number of ALB server groups that you can associate with a scaling group.

If you increase the weight of an ECS instance in ALB server group N, the number of access requests that are forwarded to the ECS instance also increases. If you set the **Weight **parameter of an ECS instance in ALB server group N to **0**, no access requests are forwarded to the ECS instance. Valid values: 0 to 100.

N specifies the serial number of the ALB server group.

The port number that is used by an ECS instance after Auto Scaling adds the ECS instance to ALB server group N. Valid values: 1 to 65535.

N specifies the serial number of the ALB server group.

>  If the N values are the same but the port numbers are different, Auto Scaling associates multiple ports of ALB server group N with the scaling group.

If you increase the weight of an ECS instance in server group N, the number of access requests that are forwarded to the ECS instance also increases. If you set the **Weight **parameter of an ECS instance in server group N to **0**, no access requests are forwarded to the ECS instance.

schema.description:
Specifies whether to evenly distribute instances in the scaling group across multiple zones. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

Default value: false.

The allocation policy of instances. Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the allocation policy to create the required number of instances. The policy can be applied to pay-as-you-go instances and preemptible instances. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified orders of the instance types to create the required number of instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPUs to create the required number of instances.

Default value: priority.

The allocation policy of preemptible instances. You can use this parameter to individually specify the allocation policy of preemptible instances. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified orders of the instance types to create the required number of preemptible instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPUs to create the required number of preemptible instances.

Default value: priority.

The maximum life span of an instance in the scaling group. Unit: seconds.

Valid values: 86400 to the value of the `Integer.maxValue` parameter.

Default value: null.

>  You cannot specify this parameter for scaling groups that manage elastic container instances or scaling groups whose ScalingPolicy parameter is set to recycle.
The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the custom scale-in policy (Function). This parameter is available only if you specify **CustomPolicy **as the value of the **RemovalPolicy.1** parameter.

The ID of the resource group to which you want to add the scaling group.

>  If you specify this parameter, new scaling groups are added to the specified resource group. If you do not specify this parameter, new scaling groups are added to the default resource group.

Weight.description:
Auto Scaling adds an ECS instance to a Server Load Balancer CLB server group, and the ECS instance is used as the weight of the backend server. The higher the weight, the more access requests the ECS instance will be assigned. If the weight is 0, the ECS instance does not receive access requests.

Value range: 0~100.

The health check method for the scaling group.  
> You can specify multiple values for this parameter to enable multiple health check options. If the `HealthCheckType` parameter is set, this parameter is ignored.

items.description:
A list of health check methods for the scaling group. Valid values:  

- NONE: No health check is performed.  
- ECS: Performs health checks on instances in the scaling group (this value enables instance health checks for both ECS and ECI scaling groups).  
- LOAD_BALANCER: Determines instance health status based on the health check results of the load balancer (Classic Load Balancer (CLB) is not supported at this time).  

Default value: ECS.

schema.description: The list of databases associated with the scaling group.

items.description: Configuration information of the databases associated with the scaling group.

Type.description:
The database type. Valid values:

- RDS
- Redis
- MongoDB

Default value: RDS.

AttachMode.description:
The join type between the scaling group and the database. Valid values:

- SecurityIp: Modifies the IP whitelist mode by automatically adding scaled-out instances to the database IP whitelist (currently supported only for RDS databases).
- SecurityGroup: Uses the security group mode by adding the scaling configuration's security group to the database's security group whitelist, enabling instances in the security group to access the database.

schema.description:
The timeout period, in seconds, for waiting until an ECS instance is successfully stopped during a scale-in process.

Valid values: 30 to 240.

> - This parameter takes effect only during scale-in operations when `ScalingPolicy` is set to `release`.  
- If this parameter is configured, the system waits up to the specified `StopInstanceTimeout` duration for the instance to stop successfully. After the timeout, scale-in proceeds regardless of whether the instance has been stopped successfully.  
- If this parameter is not configured, the system waits indefinitely for the instance to stop successfully. Scale-in continues only after successful stoppage. If stopping fails, the scale-in process rolls back and fails.
Capacity options.

OnDemandBaseCapacity.description:
The minimum number of on-demand instances required in an existing scaling group. When the number of on-demand instances in the scaling group falls below this value, the system prioritizes creating on-demand instances. Valid values: 0 to 1000.  

When the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to the `COMPOSABLE` policy, the default value is 0.

OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity.description:
The percentage of on-demand instances among the instances exceeding the minimum number of on-demand instances (`OnDemandBaseCapacity`) required by the scaling group. Valid values: 0 to 100.

When the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to the `COMPOSABLE` policy, the default value is 100.

CompensateWithOnDemand.description:
When `MultiAZPolicy` is set to `COST_OPTIMIZED`, specifies whether the system is allowed to automatically attempt to create on-demand instances to meet the required number of ECS instances if it fails to create sufficient spot instances due to price or inventory constraints. Valid values:  

- true: Allowed.  
- false: Not allowed.  

Default value: true.

SpotAutoReplaceOnDemand.description:
When `CompensateWithOnDemand` is enabled, if the proportion of on-demand instances exceeds the `OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity` threshold, the system attempts to replace excess on-demand capacity with Spot instances. This is commonly used in scenarios where `CompensateWithOnDemand` causes a fallback from Spot to on-demand instances due to Spot inventory or pricing issues. To avoid prolonged use of on-demand instances, the system tries to replace the surplus on-demand capacity with Spot instances. Valid values:

- true: Allowed.
- false: Not allowed.

Default value: false.

PriceComparisonMode.description:
The price comparison mode for the cost optimization policy of the scaling group. Valid values:

- PricePerUnit: Compares prices based on the cost per unit of capacity.

  The capacity of an instance in the scaling group equals the weight assigned to its instance type. The default weight is 1, meaning one ECS instance occupies one unit of capacity.

- PricePerVCpu: Compares prices based on the cost per vCPU.

Default value: PricePerUnit.

schema.description:
The zone balancing mode, which takes effect only when zone balancing is enabled. Valid values:
 
- BalancedBestEffort:
If resource creation fails in a zone, the system degrades to other zones to ensure best-effort resource delivery.

- BalancedOnly:
If resource creation fails in a zone, the system does not degrade to other zones. The scale-out activity partially succeeds to prevent excessive imbalance of resources across zones.

Default value: BalancedBestEffort.
schema.title: Load Balancing Mode

schema.description:
Specifies whether to enable automatic rebalancing for the scaling group. This parameter takes effect only when BalancedOnly is enabled for zone-balanced scaling groups. Valid values:

- false: disables automatic rebalancing for the scaling group.
- true: enables automatic rebalancing for the scaling group. The scaling group automatically detects capacity across zones. If the capacity is unbalanced among zones, the scaling group proactively scales in or out instances to rebalance zone capacity.

Default Value: false.

CreateScalingGroup.title: Create a scaling group
CreateScalingGroup.description:
## API Guide

A scaling group is a collection of ECS instances that share the same common scenarios.

<props="china">The number of scaling groups you can create in a region depends on your usage of automatic scaling. Go to the [Quota Center](https://quotas.console.aliyun.com/products/ess/quotas) to view the quota value corresponding to **Total Scaling Groups**.</props>

<props="intl">The number of scaling groups you can create in a region depends on your usage of automatic scaling. Go to the [Quota Center](https://quotas.console.aliyun.com/products/ess/quotas) to view the quota value corresponding to **Total Scaling Groups**.</props>

<props="partner">The number of scaling groups you can create in a region depends on your usage of automatic scaling. Go to the Quota Center to view the quota value corresponding to **Total Scaling Groups**.</props>

A scaling group does not take effect immediately after creation. You must first invoke the [EnableScalingGroup](~~25939~~) API to enable the scaling group before it can trigger scaling activities and execute scaling rules.

The scaling group, associated Classic Load Balancer (CLB, formerly SLB) instances, and associated RDS instances must reside in the same region. For more information, see [Regions and zones](~~40654~~).

If you associate a CLB instance with the scaling group, the scaling group automatically adds ECS instances that join the scaling group to the backend server group of the CLB instance. You can specify the server groups to which the ECS instances are added. Both the default server group and virtual server groups are supported, as described below:

> If you specify both the default server group and multiple virtual server groups, the ECS instances are added to all these server groups simultaneously.

- **Default server group**: ECS instances in this group receive frontend requests. If a listener is not configured with a virtual server group or a primary/secondary server group, requests are forwarded by default to the ECS instances in the default server group.
- **Virtual server group**: Use this group when you need to forward different requests to different backend servers or when you need to forward requests based on domain names and URLs.

After an ECS instance is added to the backend server group of a CLB instance, its weight defaults to 50. The CLB instance must meet the following requirements:

- The status of the CLB instance must be **active**. You can call the [DescribeLoadBalancers](~~27582~~) API to check the status of a specific CLB instance.
- Health checks must be enabled for all listener ports configured on the CLB instance. Otherwise, the scaling group fails to be created.

If you associate the scaling group with an Application Load Balancer (ALB) server group, Network Load Balancer (NLB) server group, or Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) server group, the scaling group automatically adds ECS instances that join the scaling group as backend servers of the ALB, NLB, or GWLB server group to handle access requests distributed by the ALB, NLB, or GWLB instance. You can specify multiple ALB, NLB, or GWLB server groups, but these server groups must belong to the same VPC as the scaling group. For more information, see [AttachAlbServerGroups](~~266800~~) or [AttachServerGroups](~~600535~~).

If you associate an RDS instance with the scaling group, the scaling group automatically adds the private IP addresses of ECS instances that join the scaling group to the whitelist of the RDS instance. The RDS instance must meet the following requirements:

- The status of the RDS instance must be **Running**. You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](~~26232~~) API to check the status of a specific RDS instance.
- The number of IP addresses in the RDS instance’s whitelist must not exceed the upper limit. For more information, see the RDS documentation on [Configuring a whitelist](~~43185~~).

If the `MultiAZPolicy` of the scaling group is set to `COST_OPTIMIZED`:

- When you specify the `OnDemandBaseCapacity`, `OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity`, and `SpotInstancePools` parameters—thereby defining the instance allocation method under the cost optimization policy—the scaling group prioritizes this allocation method during scale-out or scale-in operations.
- When you do not specify `OnDemandBaseCapacity`, `OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity`, or `SpotInstancePools`, the scaling group creates instances solely based on the lowest-cost option under the cost optimization policy.

If you configure propagatable tags for the scaling group—that is, when `Tag.N.Propagate` is set to `true`:

- Tags on the scaling group are propagated only to newly created instances and not to instances already running in the scaling group.
- If you specify instance tags in a scaling configuration and also choose to propagate the scaling group’s tags to the instance, all tags coexist on the instance.
- If a tag key is specified in both the scaling configuration and the propagatable tags of the scaling group, the tag value from the scaling configuration takes precedence.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling group for which you want to create the scaling rule.

The name of the scaling rule. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The name must start with a letter or a digit.

The name of a scaling rule must be unique within an Alibaba Cloud account in a region.

>  If you leave this parameter empty, the scaling rule ID is used.

The cooldown period of the scaling rule. This parameter is available only if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **SimpleScalingRule**. Valid values: 0 to 86400. Unit: seconds.

You can leave this parameter empty.

The minimum number of instances that must be scaled. This parameter takes effect if you set `ScalingRuleType` to `SimpleScalingRule` or `StepScalingRule`, and `AdjustmentType` to **PercentChangeInCapacity**.

The adjustment method of the scaling rule. If you set **ScalingRuleType** to **SimpleScalingRule** or **StepScalingRule**, you must specify this parameter. Valid values:

*   QuantityChangeInCapacity: adds the specified number of ECS instances to or removes the specified number of ECS instances from the scaling group.
*   PercentChangeInCapacity: adds the specified percentage of ECS instances to or removes the specified percentage of ECS instances from the scaling group.
*   TotalCapacity: adjusts the number of ECS instances in the scaling group to a specified number.

The number of instances that must be scaled based on the scaling rule. If you set **ScalingRuleType** to **SimpleScalingRule** or **StepScalingRule**, you must specify this parameter. The number of ECS instances that must be scaled in a scaling activity cannot exceed 1,000. Valid values of **AdjustmentValue** vary based on the value of **AdjustmentTyp****e**.

*   Valid values if **AdjustmentType** is set to **QuantityChangeInCapacity**: -1000 to 1000.
*   Valid values if **AdjustmentType** is set to **PercentChangeInCapacity**: -100 to 10000.
*   Valid values if **AdjustmentType** is set to **TotalCapacity**: 0 to 2000.

The type of the scaling rule. Valid values:

*   SimpleScalingRule: scales the number of ECS instances based on the values of **AdjustmentType** and **AdjustmentValue**.
*   TargetTrackingScalingRule: calculates the number of ECS instances that must be scaled and maintains the value of a predefined metric close to the value of **TargetValue**.
*   StepScalingRule: scales ECS instances in steps based on the specified thresholds and metric values.
*   PredictiveScalingRule: uses machine learning to analyze historical monitoring data of the scaling group and predicts the future values of metrics. In addition, Auto Scaling automatically creates scheduled tasks to specify the value range for the scaling group.

Default value: SimpleScalingRule

The warmup period of an ECS instance. This parameter is available only if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **TargetTrackingScalingRule** or **PredictiveScalingRule**. Auto Scaling adds ECS instances that are in the Warmup state to a scaling group, but does not report monitoring data of the ECS instances to CloudMonitor during the warmup period.

>  When Auto Scaling calculates the number of ECS instances that must be scaled, ECS instances in the Warmup state are not counted toward the current capacity of the scaling group.

Valid values: 0 to 86400. Unit: seconds.

Default value: 300

The predefined metric of the scaling rule. If you set **ScalingRuleType** to **TargetTrackingScalingRule** or **PredictiveScalingRule**, you must also specify this parameter.

Valid values if **ScalingRuleType** is set to **TargetTrackingScalingRule**:

*   CpuUtilization: the average CPU utilization
*   ClassicInternetRx: the average inbound Internet traffic over the classic network
*   ClassicInternetTx: the average outbound Internet traffic over the classic network
*   VpcInternetRx: the average inbound Internet traffic over a virtual private cloud (VPC)
*   VpcInternetTx: the average outbound Internet traffic over a VPC
*   IntranetRx: the average inbound traffic over the internal network
*   IntranetTx: the average outbound traffic over the internal network

Valid values if **ScalingRuleType** is set to **PredictiveScalingRule**:

*   CpuUtilization: the average CPU utilization
*   IntranetRx: the average inbound traffic over the internal network
*   IntranetTx: the average outbound traffic over the internal network

The target value. If you set **ScalingRuleType** to **TargetTrackingScalingRule** or **PredictiveScalingRule**, you must also specify this parameter. The value must be greater than 0 and can contain up to three decimal places.

Specifies whether to disable scale-in. This parameter is available if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **TargetTrackingScalingRule**.

Default value: false

The number of consecutive times that the event-triggered task created for scale-ins must meet the threshold conditions before an alert is triggered. After a target tracking scaling rule is created, an event-triggered task is automatically created and associated with the target tracking scaling rule.

Default value: 15

The number of consecutive times that the event-triggered task created for scale-outs must meet the threshold conditions before an alert is triggered. After a target tracking scaling rule is created, an event-triggered task is automatically created and associated with the target tracking scaling rule.

Default value: 3

The mode of the predictive scaling rule. Valid values:

*   PredictAndScale: provides predictions and creates prediction tasks.
*   PredictOnly: provides predictions but does not create prediction tasks.

Default value: PredictAndScale

The action on the predicted maximum value. Valid values:

*   MaxOverridePredictiveValue: uses the initial maximum capacity as the maximum value for prediction tasks if the predicted value is greater than the initial maximum capacity.
*   PredictiveValueOverrideMax: uses the predicted value as the maximum value for prediction tasks if the predicted value is greater than the initial maximum capacity.
*   PredictiveValueOverrideMaxWithBuffer: increases the predicted value by a ratio that is specified by **PredictiveValueBuffer**, and uses the increased value as the maximum value for prediction tasks if the predicted value increased by the ratio is greater than the initial maximum capacity.

Default value: MaxOverridePredictiveValue

The ratio based on which the predicted value is increased if you set **PredictiveValueBehavior** to **PredictiveValueOverrideMaxWithBuffer**. If the predicted value increased by this ratio is greater than the initial maximum capacity, the increased value is used as the maximum value for prediction tasks. Valid values: 0 to 100.

Default value: 0

The amount of buffer time before the prediction task runs. By default, all prediction tasks that are automatically created by a predictive scaling rule run on the hour. You can specify a buffer time to run prediction tasks and prepare resources in advance. Valid values: 0 to 60. Unit: minutes.

Default value: 0

The maximum number of ECS instances that can be added to the scaling group. If you specify **InitialMaxSize**, you must also specify **PredictiveValueBehavior**.

The default value of this parameter is the value of **MaxSize**.
Details of the step adjustments.

MetricIntervalUpperBound.description: The upper limit of a step adjustment. This parameter takes effect only if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **StepScalingRule**. Valid values: -9.999999E18 to 9.999999E18.

ScalingAdjustment.description: The number of ECS instances that you want to scale in each step adjustment. This parameter is available if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **StepScalingRule**.

MetricIntervalLowerBound.description: The lower limit of a step adjustment. This parameter is available if you set **ScalingRuleType** to **StepScalingRule**. Valid values: -9.999999E18 to 9.999999E18.

items.description: The upper limit that is specified in a step adjustment. Valid values: -9.999999E18 to 9.999999E18.

CreateScalingRule.title: CreateScalingRule
CreateScalingRule.description:
## API Guide

Note the following parameter-related descriptions:

- When AdjustmentType is TotalCapacity, it indicates that the number of ECS or ECI instances in the current scaling group will be adjusted to the specified quantity. The corresponding AdjustmentValue must be greater than or equal to 0.
- When AdjustmentType is QuantityChangeInCapacity or PercentChangeInCapacity, a positive AdjustmentValue indicates an increase in instances, while a negative value indicates a decrease.
- When AdjustmentType is PercentChangeInCapacity, the automatic scaling service calculates the number of ECS or ECI instances to add or remove by multiplying the current instance count (Total Capacity) by AdjustmentValue divided by 100, and then applying the round rule.
- If a cooldown time (Cooldown) is specified in the scaling rule, the scaling group enters a cooldown period for the specified duration after the scaling activity triggered by this rule completes. If no cooldown time is specified in the scaling rule, the default cooldown time (DefaultCooldown) configured for the scaling group is used instead.
- There is a limit on the number of scaling rules that can be created within a single scaling group. For details, see [Limits](~~25863~~).
- The returned unique identifier of the scaling rule (ScalingRuleAri) can be used with the following APIs:
    - Specify it in the ScalingRuleAri parameter of ExecuteScalingRule to manually execute the scaling rule.
    - Specify it in the ScheduledAction parameter of CreateScheduledTask to schedule execution of the scaling rule.

CreateScheduledTask.title: Create a scheduled task
CreateScheduledTask.description:
## API Guide

- If a scheduled task fails to trigger a scaling rule because the scaling group is undergoing a scaling activity, is disabled, or for other reasons, the scheduled task automatically retries triggering within the `LaunchExpirationTime`. Otherwise, this trigger attempt is abandoned.
- If multiple scheduled tasks trigger the same scaling group’s scaling rule at approximately the same time, the resulting scaling activities behave as follows:
    - **Scaling groups with an expected number of instances configured**: The scaling activities triggered by multiple scheduled tasks are parallel scaling activities. For example, if multiple scheduled tasks are executed within a short period, the scaling group can trigger multiple parallel scaling activities simultaneously.
    - **Scaling groups without an expected number of instances configured**: The earliest-triggered scheduled task executes its scaling activity first. Because only one scaling activity can occur in a scaling group at any given time, subsequent scheduled tasks automatically retry triggering within the `LaunchExpirationTime`. If a subsequent scheduled task is still within its `LaunchExpirationTime` when the previous scaling activity completes, its scaling rule is executed and the corresponding scaling activity is triggered.
- Scheduled tasks support the following two scaling methods:
    - Specify the scaling rule to execute by using the `ScheduledAction` parameter.
    - Set the number of instances in the scaling group by using the `ScalingGroupId` parameter.

## API Guide

If a lifecycle hook has triggered a scaling activity into the wait state, deleting the lifecycle hook will end the corresponding wait state prematurely. You can delete a lifecycle hook in one of the following two ways:

- Specify both the scaling group ID (`ScalingGroupId`) and the lifecycle hook name (`LifecycleHookName`).

The expression must conform to the Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) format, and only the operators `+ - * /` are supported.

- Maximum: The maximum value of all points in the specified interval.

Dimension.description: Metric dimension. Used to specify the resource being monitored by the metric.

DescribeAlertConfiguration.summary: When a scaling activity is executed successfully, fails, or is denied, automatic scaling supports sending notifications via text message or Email. After receiving such a message, you must handle the related management event yourself. You can invoke the DescribeAlertConfiguration API to query the statuses of scaling activities for which text message and Email Notifications are sent in a scaling group. This allows you to promptly track changes in a scaling activity and respond quickly to improve scaling efficiency.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling group.
The ID of the Region where the scaling group resides.

ScaleStatus.description: The status of scaling activities in the scaling group for which notifications are sent via text message, internal message, and Email.

items.description:
The status of scaling activities in the scaling group for which notifications are sent via text message, internal message, and Email. Possible values:

- ScaleSuccessful: A text message and Email notification were sent when the scaling activity succeeded.
- ScaleRejected: A text message and Email notification were sent when the scaling activity was denied.
- ScaleFailed: A text message and Email notification were sent when the scaling activity failed.

SpotStrategy.description:
The bidding policy for the elastic container instance. Valid values:

*   NoSpot: The instance is created as a pay-as-you-go instance.
*   SpotWithPriceLimit: The instance is created as a preemptible instance with a user-defined maximum hourly price.
*   SpotAsPriceGo: The instance is created as a preemptible instance for which the market price at the time of purchase is automatically used as the bid price.

Default value: NoSpot.

Memory.description:
The size of the memory.

You can specify the number of vCPUs and the memory size to specify the range of instance types. For example, you can set the **Cpu **parameter to 2 and the **Memory **parameter to 16 to specify the instance types that have 2 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory. If you specify the **Cpu **and **Memory **parameters, Auto Scaling determines available instance types based on factors such as I/O optimization requirements and zones. Then, Auto Scaling preferentially creates instances of the instance type that is provided at the lowest price.

>  You can specify CPU and memory specifications to create instances only if the **Scaling Policy** parameter is set to **Cost Optimization Policy** and no instance type is specified in the scaling configuration.

RestartPolicy.description:
The restart policy of the elastic container instance. Valid values:

*   Never: never restarts the elastic container instance.
*   Always: always restarts the elastic container instance.
*   OnFailure: restarts the elastic container instance upon failures.

SpotPriceLimit.description:
The maximum hourly price for the preemptible elastic container instance.

This parameter is returned only if you set the **SpotStrategy** parameter to **SpotWithPriceLimit**.

LifecycleState.description:
The state of the scaling configuration in the scaling group. Valid values:

*   Active: The scaling configuration is active in the scaling group. Auto Scaling uses the active scaling configuration to automatically create elastic container instances.
*   Inactive: The scaling configuration is inactive in the scaling group. Auto Scaling does not use the inactive scaling configuration to automatically create elastic container instances. Inactive scaling configurations are retained in the scaling group.

CostOptimization.description:
Indicates whether the cost optimization feature is enabled. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

InstanceFamilyLevel.description:
The instance family level, which is used to filter instance types that meet the requirements. This parameter is returned when the `CostOptimization` parameter is set to true. Valid values:

*   EntryLevel: shared instance type. Instances of this level are the most cost-effective but may not provide stable computing performance in a consistent manner. Instances of this level are suitable for business scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low. For more information, see [Shared instance families](~~108489~~).
*   EnterpriseLevel: Instances of this level provide stable performance and dedicated resources, and are suitable for business scenarios that require high stability. For more information, see [Instance family](~~25378~~).
*   CreditEntryLevel: This value is available only for burstable instances. CPU credits are used to ensure computing performance. Instances of this level are suitable for scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low but may fluctuate in specific cases. For more information, see [Overview](~~59977~~) of burstable instances.

items.description: The specified ECS instance type. You can specify multiple instance types (up to five). For more information, see [Create an instance by specifying an ECS instance type](~~114664~~).

DataCachePL.description:
Performance level of the disk used for data cache. We recommend using enterprise SSD (ESSD) disks. Possible values for the performance level are:

- PL0: A single disk supports up to 10,000 input/output operations per second (IOPS) for random read/write operations.
- PL1: A single disk supports up to 50,000 IOPS for random read/write operations.
- PL2: A single disk supports up to 100,000 IOPS for random read/write operations.
- PL3: A single disk supports up to 1,000,000 IOPS for random read/write operations.

> For more information about enterprise SSD (ESSD) disks, see [ESSD disks](~~122389~~).

DataCacheProvisionedIops.description:
Provisioned read/write IOPS for the ESSD AutoPL disk when it is used for data cache. Valid values: 0 to min{50,000, 1,000 × capacity − baseline performance}, where baseline performance = min{1,800 + 50 × capacity, 50,000}.
> For more information about ESSD AutoPL disks, see [ESSD AutoPL disks](~~368372~~).

DataCacheBurstingEnabled.description:
Indicates whether burst (performance burst) is enabled for data caching when using ESSD AutoPL disks. Valid values:
- true: Enabled.
- false: Disabled.

> For more information about ESSD AutoPL disks, see [ESSD AutoPL disk](~~368372~~).

DescribeLifecycleActions.title: Query Lifecycle Token
DescribeLifecycleActions.description:
## API Guide

If a scaling activity that matches the applicable type of a lifecycle hook occurs in a scaling group, each lifecycle hook triggers a lifecycle action. A lifecycle action can be in one of the following three states:

- Pending: The ECS instance is suspended.
- Timeout: The timeout period specified in the lifecycle hook has been exceeded, and the suspension of the ECS instance has ended automatically.
- Completed: You have manually ended the suspension of the ECS instance ahead of time.

If no subsequent action (for example, triggering execution of a specified OOS template after ending the suspension) was configured when creating the lifecycle hook, you can invoke this API to obtain the identifier of the lifecycle action associated with the current scaling activity, so you can customize your own subsequent action.

*   host: The ECS instance is associated with the dedicated host. If you start an ECS instance that was stopped in economical mode, the ECS instance remains on the original dedicated host. If the resources of the original dedicated host are insufficient, you cannot start the ECS instance.

The type of the private pool. A private pool is generated when an elasticity assurance or a capacity reservation takes effect. You can select a private pool for Auto Scaling to start instances. Valid values:

*   Open: open private pool. Auto Scaling selects a matching open private pool to start instances. If no matching open private pools exist, Auto Scaling uses the resources in the public pool to start instances.
*   Target: specified private pool. Auto Scaling uses the resources in the specified private pool to start instances. If the resources in the specified private pool are insufficient, instances cannot be started.
*   None: no private pool. Auto Scaling does not use the resources in private pools to start instances.

The ID of the dedicated host on which the ECS instance is created. If you specify `DedicatedHostId`, `SpotStrategy` and `SpotPriceLimit` are ignored. Because preemptible instances cannot be created on dedicated hosts.

For example, you can set CPU to 2 and Memory to 16 to specify instance types that have 2 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory. If you specify Cpu and Memory, Auto Scaling determines the available instance types based on factors such as I/O optimization requirements and zones. Instances of this level are suitable for business scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low. For more information, see [Shared instance families](~~108489~~).
*   EnterpriseLevel: Instances of this level provide stable performance and dedicated resources, and are suitable for business scenarios that require high stability. For more information, see [Instance family](~~25378~~).
*   CreditEntryLevel: This value is valid only for burstable instances. CPU credits are used to ensure computing performance. Instances of this level are suitable for scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low but may fluctuate in specific cases. For more information, see the [Overview](~~59977~~) topic of burstable instances.

CustomPriority.description:
The custom priority for combinations of **ECS instance type + virtual switch**.

> This parameter takes effect only when the scaling group's **scaling policy** is set to `priority policy`.

If the system cannot create an ECS instance using a combination with a higher priority (**ECS instance type + virtual switch**), the automatic scaling service automatically selects the next highest-priority combination to create the ECS instance.

> If custom priorities are specified only for certain **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combinations, the unspecified combinations have lower priority than the specified ones. Among the unspecified combinations, priority is determined sequentially based on the order of virtual switches in the scaling group and the order of instance types in the scaling configuration. For example, if the scaling group's virtual switch order is vsw1, vsw2, and the scaling configuration's instance type order is type1, type2, and the custom priority order is `["vsw2+type2", "vsw1+type2"]`, then the final priority order is `vsw2+type2` > `vsw1+type2` > `vsw1+type1` > `vsw2+type1`.

If no private pool is specified or the specified private pools lack sufficient capacity, the system automatically matches open-type private pools. If no eligible private pool is available, instances are created using the public pool.

MultiAZPolicy.description:
The scaling policy for the multi-zone scaling group that contains ECS instances. Valid values:

*   PRIORITY: ECS instances are created based on the value of the VSwitchIds.N parameter. If Auto Scaling fails to create ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the highest priority resides, Auto Scaling creates ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the next highest priority resides.

*   COST_OPTIMIZED: ECS instances are created based on the unit price of vCPUs. Auto Scaling preferentially creates ECS instances whose vCPUs have the lowest price. If you specified preemptible instance types in the scaling configuration, Auto Scaling preferentially creates preemptible instances. You can use the **CompensateWithOnDemand** parameter to specify whether to automatically create pay-as-you-go instances when preemptible instances cannot be created due to insufficient resources.

    **

    **Note** The COST_OPTIMIZED setting takes effect only when multiple instance types are specified or preemptible instances are used.

*   BALANCE: ECS instances are evenly distributed across the zones that are specified for the scaling group. If ECS instances are unevenly distributed across zones due to insufficient resources, you can call the [RebalanceInstance](~~71516~~) operation to evenly redistribute the instances across the zones.

*   COMPOSABLE: You can combine the preceding policies based on your business requirements.

The processes that are suspended. If no process is suspended, null is returned. Valid values:

- ScaleIn: scale-in
- ScaleOut: scale-out
- HealthCheck: health check
- AlarmNotification: event-triggered task
- ScheduledAction: scheduled task

SystemSuspended.description:
Indicates whether Auto Scaling stops executing scaling activities in the scaling group. Valid values:

- true: If the scaling activities fail for more than seven consecutive days, Auto Scaling stops executing scaling activities in the scaling group. You must modify the scaling group or scaling configuration to resume the execution of the scaling activities.
- false: Auto Scaling does not stop executing scaling activities in the scaling group.

MonitorGroupId.description: The ID of the CloudMonitor application group that is associated with the scaling group.

AzBalance.description:
Specifies whether to evenly distribute instances in the scaling group across zones. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

Default value: false.

AllocationStrategy.description:
The allocation policy of instances. Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the allocation policy to create the required number of instances. The policy can be applied to pay-as-you-go instances and preemptible instances. This parameter takes effect only when you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified order of the instance types to create the required number of instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPUs to create the required number of instances.

Default value: priority.

SpotAllocationStrategy.description:
The allocation policy of preemptible instances. You can use this parameter to individually specify the allocation policy of preemptible instances. This parameter takes effect only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified order of the instance types to create the required number of preemptible instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPUs to create the required number of preemptible instances.

Default value: priority.

MaxInstanceLifetime.description:
The maximum life span of an instance in the scaling group. Unit: seconds.

Valid values: 86400 to the value of the Integer.maxValue parameter.

Default value: null.

CustomPolicyARN.description: The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the custom scale-in policy (Function). This parameter is available only if you specify CustomPolicy as the first step to remove instances.

InitCapacity.description: The number of instances that are in the Initialized state before the instances are added to the scaling group.

ResourceGroupId.description: The ID of the resource group to which the ECS instance belongs.

LoadBalancerId.description: The IDs of the SLB instances that are associated with the scaling group.

Weight.description: The weight of an ECS instance after Auto Scaling adds the ECS instance to the ALB server group as a backend server.

items.description: The list of Classic Load Balancer (CLB, formerly known as SLB) configurations.

EnableDesiredCapacity.description:
Indicates whether the expected number of instances identity is enabled. Valid values:
- true: Enabled. The query result of the scaling group includes the expected number of instances.
- false: Disabled. The query result of the scaling group does not include the expected number of instances.

Tag.description: The collection of tags for the scaling group.

items.description: The collection of tag information for the scaling group.

TagKey.description: The tag key of the scaling group.

TagValue.description: The tag value of the scaling group.

Propagate.description:
Indicates whether the tag is propagatable. Possible values:  

- true: The tag on the scaling group is propagated only to newly created instances, not to instances already running in the scaling group.  
- false: The tag on the scaling group is not propagated to instances.  

Default value: false.

HealthCheckType.description:
The health check method for the scaling group. Valid values:

- NONE: No health check is performed.
- ECS: Performs health checks on instances in the scaling group (this value enables instance health checks for both ECS and ECI scaling groups).
- LOAD_BALANCER: Determines the health status of instances based on the health check results from the load balancer (CLB load balancing type is not supported yet).

items.description:
The health check method for the scaling group. Valid values:

- NONE: No health check is performed.
- ECS: Performs health checks on instances in the scaling group (this value enables instance health checks for both ECS and ECI scaling groups).
- LOAD_BALANCER: Determines the health status of instances based on the health check results from the load balancer (CLB load balancing type is not supported yet).

DBInstance.description: The list of databases associated with the scaling group.

items.description: The configuration information of the databases associated with the scaling group.

Type.description:
The database type. Valid values:

- RDS.
- Redis.
- MongoDB.

SecurityGroupId.description: The whitelist of security groups that the scaling group adds to the database.

items.description:
Indicates whether the scaling group removes the security groups in the associated database list from the database security group whitelist. This setting takes effect only when the `AttachMode` parameter in the CreateScalingGroup API is set to `SecurityGroup`. Valid values:  

- true: The security groups in this list are removed from the database security group whitelist.  
- false: The security groups in this list are not removed from the database security group whitelist.

SpotCapacity.description: The number of spot instances in the scaling group.

StopInstanceTimeout.description: The timeout period, in seconds, to wait for an ECS instance to stop successfully during a scale-in flow.

OnDemandBaseCapacity.description: The minimum number of on-demand instances required in an existing scaling group. When the number of on-demand instances in the scaling group is less than this value, the system prioritizes creating on-demand instances. Valid values: 0 to 1000.

OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity.description: The percentage of on-demand instances among the instances exceeding the minimum number of on-demand instances (`OnDemandBaseCapacity`) required by the scaling group. Valid values: 0 to 100.

CompensateWithOnDemand.description:
When `MultiAZPolicy` is set to `COST_OPTIMIZED`, specifies whether the system is allowed to automatically attempt to create on-demand instances to meet the required number of ECS instances if it cannot create enough spot instances due to factors such as price or inventory. Valid values:

- true: Allowed.
- false: Not allowed.

SpotAutoReplaceOnDemand.description:
When `CompensateWithOnDemand` is enabled, if the proportion of on-demand instances exceeds the `OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity` threshold, the system attempts to replace excess on-demand capacity with Spot instances. This is commonly used in scenarios where `CompensateWithOnDemand` causes a fallback from Spot to on-demand instances due to Spot inventory or pricing issues. To prevent on-demand instances from remaining active for extended periods, the system tries to replace surplus on-demand capacity with Spot instances. Valid values:

- true: Allowed.
- false: Not allowed.

PriceComparisonMode.description:
The price comparison mode for the scaling group's cost optimization policy. Valid values:

- PricePerUnit: Compares prices based on the price per unit of capacity.

  The capacity contribution of an instance in the scaling group equals the weight assigned to its instance type, which defaults to 1 (meaning one ECS instance contributes a capacity of 1).

- PricePerVCpu: Compares prices based on the price per vCPU.

Default value: PricePerUnit.

BalanceMode.description:
Zone balance mode, which takes effect only when zone balance mode is enabled. Valid values:

- BalancedBestEffort:
If resource creation fails in a zone, the system degrades to other zones to ensure best-effort delivery of resources.

- BalancedOnly:
If resource creation fails in a zone, the system does not degrade to other zones. The scale-out activity is partially successful to prevent excessive imbalance of resources across different zones.
BalanceMode.title: Load balancing mode

AutoRebalance.description:
Specifies whether to enable automatic rebalancing for the scaling group. This setting takes effect only when BalancedOnly is enabled for a zone-balanced scaling group. Valid values:
- false: Disables automatic rebalancing for the scaling group.
- true: Enables automatic rebalancing. When enabled, the scaling group automatically monitors capacity distribution across zones and proactively scales in or out in specific zones to rebalance capacity when imbalance is detected.
AutoRebalance.title: Auto Rebalance Scaling Group

schema.description: The region ID of the scaling group.
The ID of the scaling group.
The ID of the associated scaling configuration.

The health status of the ECS instance in the scaling group. If ECS instances do not run as expected, Auto Scaling considers the ECS instances unhealthy. Valid values:

*   Healthy
*   Unhealthy

Auto Scaling automatically removes unhealthy ECS instances from the scaling group and then releases automatically created instances among the unhealthy instances.

Unhealthy ECS instances that are manually added to the scaling group are released based on the management mode of the instance lifecycles. If the lifecycles of the ECS instances are not managed by the scaling group, Auto Scaling removes the instances from the scaling group but does not release the instances. If the lifecycles of the ECS instances are managed by the scaling group, Auto Scaling removes the instances from the scaling group and releases the instances.

>  Make sure that you have sufficient balance within your Alibaba Cloud account. If you have overdue payments within your Alibaba Cloud account, pay-as-you-go and preemptible instances are stopped or released. For information about how the states of ECS instances with overdue payments change, see [Overdue payments](~~170589~~).

The lifecycle state of the ECS instance in the scaling group. Valid values:

*   InService: The ECS instance is added to the scaling group and provides services as expected.
*   Pending: The ECS instance is being added to the scaling group. During this process, Auto Scaling adds the ECS instance to the backend server groups of the associated Classic Load Balancer (CLB) instance and adds the private IP address of the ECS instance to the IP address whitelist of the associated ApsaraDB RDS instance.
*   Pending:Wait: The ECS instance is waiting to be added to the scaling group. If a lifecycle hook that applies to scale-out activities is created for the scaling group, the ECS instance enters the Pending:Wait state. The ECS instance is added to the scaling group only after the lifecycle hook times out.
*   Protected: The ECS instance is being protected. The ECS instance can provide services as expected. However, Auto Scaling does not manage the lifecycle of the ECS instance. You must manually manage the lifecycle of the ECS instance.
*   Standby: The ECS instance is on standby. The ECS instance is out of service and the weight of the ECS instance as a backend server is set to zero. Auto Scaling does not manage the lifecycle of the ECS instance. You must manually manage the lifecycle of the ECS instance.
*   Stopped: The ECS instance is stopped. The ECS instance is stopped and cannot provide services.
*   Removing: The ECS instance is being removed from the scaling group. During this process, Auto Scaling removes the ECS instance from the backend server groups of the associated CLB instance and removes the IP address of the ECS instance from the IP address whitelist of the associated ApsaraDB RDS instance.
*   Removing:Wait: The ECS instance is waiting to be removed from the scaling group. If a lifecycle hook that applies to scale-in activities is created for the scaling group, the ECS instance enters the Removing:Wait state. The ECS instance is removed from the scaling group only after the lifecycle hook times out.

Specifies how the ECS instance is created. Valid values:

*   AutoCreated: The ECS instance is automatically created by Auto Scaling based on the instance configuration source of the scaling group.
*   Attached: The ECS instance is manually added to the scaling group.

schema.description: A list of lifecycle states of ECS instances, ECI instances, or managed instances in the scaling group. You can specify either this parameter or the `LifecycleState` parameter, but not both. We recommend that you use this parameter.

items.description:
The lifecycle state of an ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance in the scaling group. Valid values:

- InService: The instance has been successfully added to the scaling group and is providing services normally.
- Pending: The instance is being added. This process includes adding the instance to the backend server group of an SLB instance and the whitelist of an RDS instance.
- Pending:Wait: The instance is suspended during the addition process. If a lifecycle hook for scale-out activities exists in the scaling group, the instance is suspended and waits until the hook timeout period ends.
- Protected: The instance is providing services normally, but its lifecycle is manually managed by you instead of by automatic scaling.
- Standby: The instance is not providing services (its weight of SLB backend server is set to zero), and its lifecycle is manually managed by you instead of by automatic scaling.
- Stopped: The instance is stopped and not providing services.
- Removing: The instance is being removed. This process includes removing the instance from the backend server group of an SLB instance and the whitelist of an RDS instance.
- Removing:Wait: The instance is suspended during the removal process. If a lifecycle hook for scale-down activities exists in the scaling group, the instance is suspended and waits until the hook timeout period ends.

> Managed instances do not support lifecycle hooks, association with load balancing, or health check features.

The weight of the SLB instance.

LaunchTemplateId.description: The ID of the launch template.

SpotStrategy.description:
The spot strategy for the spot instance. Valid values:  
- SpotWithPriceLimit: A spot instance with a specified maximum price.  
- SpotAsPriceGo: The system automatically bids based on the current market price.

LaunchTemplateVersion.description: The version of the launch template used by the instance.

HealthStatus.description:
The health status of the ECS instance or ECI instance in the scaling group. An ECS instance or ECI instance that is not in the running state is considered unhealthy. Valid values: 

- Healthy: The ECS instance or ECI instance is healthy.
- Unhealthy: The ECS instance or ECI instance is unhealthy.

Automatic scaling automatically removes unhealthy ECS instances or ECI instances from the scaling group and releases those that were automatically created.

Whether a manually added ECS instance or ECI instance is released depends on its lifecycle management status. If the instance lifetime is not managed by the scaling group, the instance is only removed but not released. If the instance lifetime is managed by the scaling group, the instance is both removed and released.

> Ensure that your account has sufficient available credit. If your account has an overdue payment, all pay-as-you-go ECS instances or ECI instances (including pay-as-you-go instances and spot instances) will be stopped and may even be released. For information about how the status of ECS instances or ECI instances in a scaling group changes after an overdue payment, see [Overdue payments](~~170589~~).

ScalingGroupId.description: The ID of the scaling group to which the instance belongs.

WarmupState.description:
The prefetch status of the instance. Valid values:  
- NoNeedWarmup: Prefetch is not required.  
- WaitingForInstanceWarmup: Waiting for prefetch to complete.  
- InstanceWarmupFinish: Prefetch has completed.

LifecycleState.description:
The lifecycle state of an ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance in the scaling group. Valid values:

- InService: The instance has been successfully added to the scaling group and is providing services normally.
- Pending: The instance is being added. This process includes adding the ECS instance or ECI instance to the backend servers of an SLB instance and the whitelist of an RDS instance.
- Pending:Wait: The instance addition is suspended. If a lifecycle hook for scale-out activities is configured in the scaling group, the ECS instance or ECI instance is suspended during the addition process and waits until the hook timeout period ends.
- Protected: The instance is protected. The ECS instance or ECI instance provides services normally, but its lifecycle is not managed by automatic scaling; instead, you manage it manually.
- Standby: The instance is on standby. The ECS instance or ECI instance does not provide services, its weight of SLB backend server is set to zero, and its lifecycle is not managed by automatic scaling; instead, you manage it manually.
- Stopped: The instance is stopped. The ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance is powered off and does not provide services.
- Removing: The instance is being removed. This process includes removing the ECS instance or ECI instance from the backend servers of an SLB instance and the whitelist of an RDS instance.
- Removing:Wait: The instance removal is suspended. If a lifecycle hook for scale-down activities is configured in the scaling group, the ECS instance or ECI instance is suspended during the removal process and waits until the hook timeout period ends.

> Managed instances do not support lifecycle hooks, association with load balancing, or health check features.

CreationType.description:
The creation method of the instance in the scaling group. Valid values:

- AutoCreated: An ECS instance automatically created by automatic scaling based on the instance configuration information source.
- Attached: An ECS instance not created by the automatic scaling service but manually added to the scaling group by you.
- Managed: A managed instance not created by the automatic scaling service but manually added to the scaling group by you.

- false: The instance is not entrusted to the scaling group.

*   TargetTrackingScalingRule: calculates the number of ECS instances that must be scaled and maintains the value of a predefined metric close to the value of **TargetValue**.

The predefined metric of the scaling rule. If you set **ScalingRuleType** to **TargetTrackingScalingRule** or **PredictiveScalingRule**, you must specify this parameter.

Valid values if **ScalingRuleType** is set to **TargetTrackingScalingRule**:

*   CpuUtilization: the average CPU utilization

*   ClassicInternetRx: the average inbound Internet traffic over the classic network

*   ClassicInternetTx: the average outbound Internet traffic over the classic network

*   VpcInternetRx: the average inbound Internet traffic over a virtual private cloud (VPC)

*   VpcInternetTx: the average outbound Internet traffic over a VPC

*   IntranetRx: the average inbound traffic over the internal network

*   IntranetTx: the average outbound traffic over the internal network

    Valid values if **ScalingRuleType** is set to **PredictiveScalingRule**:

AdjustmentType.description:
The adjustment method of the scaling rule. Valid values:

*   QuantityChangeInCapacity: adds the specified number of ECS instances to or removes the specified number of ECS instances from the scaling group.
*   PercentChangeInCapacity: adds the specified percentage of ECS instances to or removes the specified percentage of ECS instances from the scaling group.

*   PredictAndScale: provides predictions and creates prediction tasks.

MinAdjustmentMagnitude.description: The minimum number of instances that must be scaled. This parameter takes effect only if you set `ScalingRuleType` to `SimpleScalingRule` or `StepScalingRule`, and `AdjustmentType` to **PercentChangeInCapacity**.

By default, all prediction tasks that are automatically created by a predictive scaling rule run on the hour. You can specify a buffer time to run prediction tasks and prepare resources in advance. Valid values: 0 to 60. Unit: minutes.

*   PredictiveValueOverrideMaxWithBuffer: increases the predicted value by a ratio that is specified by **PredictiveValueBuffer**, and uses the increased value as the maximum value for prediction tasks if the predicted value increased by the ratio is greater than the initial maximum capacity.

DetachInstances.title: Remove one or more ECS instances from a scaling group
DetachInstances.description:
## API Guide

- Before invoking this API, ensure that the following conditions are met:
    - The target scaling group must be in the Enabled state.
    - The target scaling group must not have any ongoing scaling activities.

       > When no scaling activity is in progress for the target scaling group, this API can bypass the cooldown time and directly trigger a scaling activity.

- Note the following when using this API:
    - After an ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance is removed, it continues to exist independently of the scaling group. You can call the [AttachInstances](~~25954~~) API to add the ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance to another scaling group again.
    - Removing an ECS instance, ECI instance, or managed instance via this API does not stop or release the instance.
    - A successful API call only indicates that the automatic scaling service has accepted the request. Although a scaling activity can be triggered normally, successful execution of the scaling activity is not guaranteed. You must check the status of the scaling activity by using the returned ScalingActivityId.
    - The number of ECS instances, ECI instances, or managed instances in the target scaling group minus the number of instances being removed must not be less than the minimum instance count (MinSize) of the scaling group; otherwise, an error occurs.

InstanceType.description:
If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of instance types, you must specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType and LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameters at the same time.

This parameter specifies instance type N that overrides the instance type specified in the launch template. You can specify N instance types in the extended configurations of the launch template. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  This parameter takes effect only when the LaunchTemplateId parameter is specified.

For information about the valid values of InstanceType in InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType, see [Instance families](~~25378~~).

WeightedCapacity.description:
If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of instance types, you must specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter after you specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType parameter. The two parameters have a one-to-one correspondence. The value of N in the two parameters must be the same.

This parameter specifies the weight of the instance type. The weight specifies the capacity of a single instance of the specified instance type in the scaling group. A higher weight specifies that a smaller number of instances of the specified instance type are required to meet the expected capacity.

Performance metrics such as the number of vCPUs and the memory size of each instance type may vary. You can specify different weights for different instance types based on your business requirements.

Examples:

*   Current capacity: 0
*   Expected capacity: 6
*   Capacity of ecs.c5.xlarge: 4

To meet the expected capacity, Auto Scaling creates two ecs.c5.xlarge instances.

>  The capacity of the scaling group cannot exceed the sum of the maximum capacity that is specified by MaxSize and the maximum weight of the instance type.

Valid values of WeightedCapacity in LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity: 1 to 500.

EnableScalingGroup.title: Enable a scaling group
EnableScalingGroup.description:
## API Guide

- You can invoke this API to enable a scaling group only when the scaling group is in the Inactive state and has a valid source of instance configuration information configured (such as a scaling configuration, a launch template, or ECS instances specified during scaling group creation). Otherwise, the invocation fails.

    > A scaling group can have only one active source of instance configuration information at any given time. When invoking this API, you can specify a scaling configuration or a launch template for the scaling group. If an instance configuration source was already configured for the scaling group before invoking this API, specifying a scaling configuration or launch template during the invocation will overwrite the existing configuration.

- If you specify ECS instances to add to the scaling group by using the InstanceId.N parameter, after the API call, the automatic scaling service checks whether the total number of ECS instances in the scaling group (Total Capacity) falls within the range defined by the minimum (MinSize) and maximum (MaxSize) values:

    - If the Total Capacity is less than MinSize, after a successful invocation, the automatic scaling service automatically creates the required number of pay-as-you-go ECS instances to meet the MinSize requirement.

      For example: When creating a scaling group, you set MinSize to 5. When enabling the scaling group, you specify two existing ECS instances via the InstanceId.N parameter. After adding these two instances, the automatic scaling service automatically creates three additional ECS instances.

    - If the Total Capacity exceeds MaxSize, the invocation fails.

EnterStandby.title: Set ECS instances in a scaling group to the standby state
EnterStandby.description:
## API Guide

- If the scaling group is associated with an SLB instance, the weight of the corresponding instance in the SLB instance is set to 0.

- When an instance is in the standby state, you can manually remove it from the scaling group and release it as normal.

- Scaling activities triggered by changes in the number of instances in the scaling group or by monitoring jobs will not remove instances that are in the standby state.

- When an instance is in the standby state and enters an unhealthy state (for example, stopping or restarting), its health check status is not updated, and no scaling activity is triggered to remove unhealthy instances. The health check status is only updated again after the instance exits the standby state.

ExecuteScalingRule.title: Execute a scaling rule
ExecuteScalingRule.description:
# API Guide
When invoking this API, note the following:
- Before invoking this API, ensure that the following conditions are met:

    - The scaling group is in the `Active` state.
    - The scaling group has no scaling activity in progress.

- If the scaling group has no scaling activity in progress, this API can bypass the cooldown time and directly execute a scaling activity.

- If the number of ECS instances to be added by the scaling rule plus the current total capacity of the scaling group exceeds the maximum instance count (MaxSize), the scaling activity will be executed with Total Capacity set to MaxSize.

- If the current total capacity of the scaling group minus the number of ECS instances to be removed by the scaling rule is less than the minimum instance count (MinSize), the scaling activity will be executed with Total Capacity set to MinSize.

A successful response from this API only indicates that the automatic scaling service has accepted the request and can proceed with the scaling activity. It does not guarantee that the scaling activity will succeed. You must use the returned `ScalingActivityId` to check the execution status of the scaling activity.
> There is a limit on the number of ECS instances that can be adjusted in a single operation. For more information, see the description of the AdjustmentValue parameter in [CreateScalingRule](~~25948~~).

ExitStandby.title: Bring instances in standby state into running state
ExitStandby.description:
## API Guide

After an instance is removed from the standby state in a scaling group, note the following:

- The ECS instance or ECI instance transitions to the running state (that is, recovers to the service state).

- If the scaling group to which the ECS instance or ECI instance belongs is associated with an SLB instance, the ECS instance or ECI instance rejoins the SLB instance with a default weight of 50.

- If the ECS instance or ECI instance is stopped or restarted, its health check status is updated again.

- During a scale-in scaling activity, automatic scaling can remove the ECS instance or ECI instance from the scaling group.

schema.description: The region ID of the event-triggered task.
The ID of the event-triggered task.
The name of the event-triggered task.
The description of the event-triggered task.

The name of the metric. The valid values vary based on the metric type.

*   If you set **MetricType** to **custom**, the valid values are your custom metrics.

*   If you set **MetricType** to **system**, the **MetricName** parameter has the following valid values:

    *   **CpuUtilization**: the CPU utilization of an ECS instance. Unit: %.
    *   **IntranetTx**: the outbound traffic over the internal network from an ECS instance. Unit: KB/min.
    *   **IntranetRx**: the inbound traffic over the Internet to an ECS instance that resides in a virtual private cloud (VPC). Unit: KB/min.
    *   **VpcInternetTx**: the outbound traffic over the Internet from an ECS instance that resides in a VPC. Unit: KB/min.
    *   **VpcInternetRx**: the inbound traffic over the Internet to an ECS instance that resides in a VPC. Unit: KB/min.
    *   **SystemDiskReadBps**: the number of bytes read from the system disk used by an ECS instance per second.
    *   **SystemDiskWriteBps**: the number of bytes written to the system disk used by an ECS instance per second.
    *   **SystemDiskReadOps**: the number of read operations on the system disk used by an ECS instance per second.
    *   **SystemDiskWriteOps**: the number of write operations on the system disk used by an ECS instance per second.
    *   **CpuUtilizationAgent**: the CPU utilization of an agent. Unit: %.
    *   **GpuUtilizationAgent**: the GPU utilization of an agent. Unit: %.
    *   **GpuMemoryFreeUtilizationAgent**: the percentage of idle GPU memory of an agent.
    *   **GpuMemoryUtilizationAgent**: the GPU memory usage of an agent. Unit: %.
    *   **MemoryUtilization**: the memory usage of an agent. Unit: %.
    *   **LoadAverage**: the average system load of an agent.
    *   **TcpConnection**: the total number of TCP connections of an agent.
    *   **TcpConnection**: the number of established TCP connections of an agent.
    *   **PackagesNetOut**: the number of packets that are sent by the internal network interface controller (NIC) used by an agent.
    *   **PackagesNetIn**: the number of packets that are received by the internal NIC used by an agent.
    *   **EciPodCpuUtilization**: the CPU utilization of an elastic container instance. Unit: %.
    *   **EciPodMemoryUtilization**: the memory usage of an elastic container instance. Unit: %.

For more information, see [Event-triggered task for system monitoring](~~74854~~).

The type of the metric. Valid values:

*   system: system metrics of CloudMonitor
*   custom: custom metrics that are reported to CloudMonitor

The period during which the statistical value of the metric is collected. Unit: seconds. Valid values:

*   15

*   60

*   120

*   300

*   900

    **

    **Note** If your scaling group is of the ECS type and the event-triggered task associated with your scaling group monitors CloudMonitor metrics, you can set the **Period** parameter to **15**. Otherwise, you can set the **Period **parameter to **60**, **120**, **300**, or **900**. In most cases, the name of a CloudMonitor metric contains Agent.

The method that is used to collect statistics about the metric. Valid values:

*   Average
*   Minimum
*   Maximum
The threshold of the metric value. If the threshold is reached *N* times within the specified period, a scaling rule is executed.

The operator that is used to compare the metric value and the threshold.

*   If the metric value is greater than or equal to the threshold, set the value to `>=`.
*   If the metric value is less than or equal to the threshold, set the value to `<=`.
*   If the metric value is greater than the threshold, set the value to `>`.
*   If the metric value is less than the threshold, set the value to `<`.

The number of times that the threshold must be reached before a scaling rule can be executed. For example, if you set this parameter to **3**, the average CPU utilization must reach or exceed 80% three times in a row before a scaling rule is triggered.
The ID of the application group to which the custom metric belongs. If you set the **MetricType** parameter to **custom**, you must specify this parameter.

The effective period of the event-triggered task.

This parameter follows the cron expression format. The default format is `X X X X X ?`, in which:

*   X: a placeholder for a field, which represents seconds, minutes, hours, days, and months in sequence. X can be a definite value or a special character that has logical meaning. For information about the valid values of X, see [Cron expression](~~25907~~).
*   ?: No value is specified.

>  **By default, the value of this parameter is specified in UTC+8**. You can specify the time zone before a cron expression in the `TZ=+yy` format. y indicates the time zone. For example, `TZ=+00 * * 1-2 * * ?` specifies that the event-triggered task is in effect between 01:00 and 02:59 (UTC+0) every day.

Sample values:

*   ` * * * * * ?  `: The event-triggered task is in effect all the time.
*   ` * * 17-18 * * ?  `: The event-triggered task is in effect between 17:00 and 18:59 (UTC+8) every day.
*   `TZ=+00 * * 1-2 * * ?`: The event-triggered task is in effect between 01:00 and 02:59 (UTC+0) every day.
The unique identifiers of the scaling rules that are associated with the event-triggered task.

DimensionKey.description:
The key of dimension *N* that is associated with the metric. The valid values vary based on the metric type.

*   If you set **MetricType** to **custom**, you can specify this parameter based on your business requirements.

*   If you set **MetricType** to **system**, this parameter has the following valid values:

    *   **user_id**: the ID of your Alibaba Cloud account
    *   **scaling_group**: the scaling group that you want to monitor
    *   **device**: the type of the NIC
    *   **state**: the status of the TCP connection

DimensionValue.description:
The value of dimension *N *that is associated with the metric. The valid values vary based on the value of **Dimension.N.DimensionKey**.

*   If you set **Dimension.N.DimensionKey** to a custom value, you can specify this parameter based on your business requirements.

*   If the value of **Dimension.N.DimensionKey** is specified by the system, this parameter has the following valid values:

    *   **user_id**: The system specifies the value.

    *   **scaling_group**: The system specifies the value.

    *   **device**: You can set this parameter to **eth0 **or **eth1**.

        *   For instances that reside in the classic network type, **eth0 **specifies the internal NIC. Only one eth0 NIC exists on each instance that resides in a VPC.
        *   For instances that reside in the classic network, **eth1 **specifies the public NIC.

    *   **state**: You can set this parameter to **TCP_TOTAL **or **ESTABLISHED**.

        *   **TCP_TOTAL **specifies the total number of TCP connections.
        *   **ESTABLISHED **specifies the number of established TCP connections.
