ModifyAlarm.title: ModifyAlarm
ModifyAlarm.description:
## API Guide

- If you create an event-triggered task of the custom monitoring type (MetricType=custom), you must first report the custom monitoring metric to CloudMonitor. For more information, see [Event-Triggered Tasks for Custom Monitoring](~~74861~~).

- When creating an event-triggered task, you must specify a metric (MetricName) and provide dimension information (`Dimension.N.DimensionKey` and `Dimension.N.DimensionValue`) to define the aggregation scope of the metric data within the scaling group. For example, specify `user_id` and `scaling_group` to aggregate metric data across all ECS instances or ECI instances under the specified user and scaling group.
    - The metrics available for custom monitoring event-triggered tasks (MetricType=custom) depend on your own custom metrics.
    - For more information about metrics supported by system monitoring event-triggered tasks (MetricType=system), see [Event-Triggered Tasks for System Monitoring](~~74854~~).

> In the dimension information, `user_id` and `scaling_group` are automatically filled by the system, while `device` and `state` must be manually specified by you. For more information, see the parameters `Dimension.N.DimensionKey` and `Dimension.N.DimensionValue`.

ModifyAlertConfiguration.summary: When a scaling activity is executed successfully, fails, or is denied, automatic scaling supports sending notifications via text message or Email. After receiving such a message, you must handle the related management event yourself. You can invoke the API ModifyAlertConfiguration to configure the scaling activity statuses for which text message or Email notifications should be sent in a scaling group. This allows you to stay promptly informed about changes in scaling activities and respond quickly to improve scaling efficiency.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling group.
The Region ID of the scaling group.
The scaling activity statuses in the scaling group for which text message or Email notifications should be sent.

items.description:
The scaling activity statuses in the scaling group for which text message or Email notifications should be sent. Valid values:

- ScaleSuccessful: Send a text message or Email notification when the scaling activity executes successfully.
- ScaleRejected: Send a text message or Email notification when the scaling activity is denied.
- ScaleFailed: Send a text message or Email notification when the scaling activity fails.

>If this parameter is not set (that is, the parameter is empty), all text message and Email notifications are canceled.

ModifyEciScalingConfiguration.summary: Invoke ModifyScalingConfiguration to modify a scaling configuration of Elastic Container Instance (ECI) type.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling configuration that you want to modify.

The name of the scaling configuration. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The name must start with a letter or a digit.

The name of the scaling configuration must be unique within a scaling group in a region. If you do not specify this parameter, the value of the ScalingConfigurationId parameter is used.

The ID of the security group with which you want to associate the elastic container instance. Elastic container instances that are associated with the same security group can communicate with each other.

If you do not specify a security group, the system uses the default security group in the region that you select. Make sure that the inbound rules of the security group contain the protocols and the port numbers of the containers that you want to expose. If you do not have a default security group in the region, the system automatically creates a default security group and adds the declared container protocols and port numbers to the inbound rules of the security group.

The name of the elastic container instance. The name must meet the following requirements:

*   The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length.
*   The name can contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-). The name cannot start or end with a hyphen (-).

The restart policy of the elastic container instance. Valid values:

*   Always: always restarts the elastic container instance.
*   Never: never restarts the elastic container instance.
*   OnFailure: restarts the elastic container instance upon failures.

Default value: Always.
The number of vCPUs of the elastic container instance.
The memory size of the elastic container instance. Unit: GiB.
The ID of the resource group.

The Domain Name System (DNS) policy. Valid values:

schema.description: The ID of the lifecycle hook that you want to modify.
The ID of the scaling group to which the lifecycle hook belongs.
The name of the lifecycle hook that you want to modify.

The action that Auto Scaling performs after the lifecycle hook times out. Valid values:

*   CONTINUE: Auto Scaling continues to respond to a scale-in or scale-out request.
*   ABANDON: Auto Scaling releases Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances that are created during scale-out activities or removes ECS instances from the scaling group during scale-in activities.
*   ROLLBACK: For scale-in activities, Auto Scaling rejects the requests to release ECS instances but rolls back ECS instances. For scale-out activities, the ROLLBACK setting has the same effect as the ABANDON setting.

If a scaling group has multiple lifecycle hooks in effect and you set the `DefaultResult` parameter for one of the lifecycle hooks to `ABANDON` or `ROLLBACK`, the following rule applies to scale-in activities: When the lifecycle hook whose **DefaultResult** parameter is set to **ABANDON** or **ROLLBACK** times out, other lifecycle hooks time out ahead of schedule. In other cases, Auto Scaling performs the action only after the last lifecycle hook times out.

The period of time before the lifecycle hook times out. When the lifecycle hook times out, Auto Scaling performs the action that is specified by the **DefaultResult **parameter. Valid values: 30 to 21600. Unit: seconds.

You can call the [RecordLifecycleActionHeartbeat](~~73846~~) operation to extend the period of time before a lifecycle hook times out. You can also call the [CompleteLifecycleAction](~~73847~~) operation to end a lifecycle hook ahead of schedule.

The type of the scaling activity to which the lifecycle hook applies. Valid values:

*   SCALE_OUT: scale-out activity
*   SCALE_IN: scale-in activity

The fixed string that is included in a notification that Auto Scaling sends when the lifecycle hook takes effect. The value of this parameter cannot exceed 4,096 characters in length.

Auto Scaling sends the value of the `NotificationMetadata` parameter together with the notification. This helps you categorize your notifications. If you specify the `NotificationMetadata` parameter, you must specify the `NotificationArn` parameter.

The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the notification method.

*   If you use a Message Service (MNS) queue as the notification method, specify the value in the `acs:mns:{region-id}:{account-id}:queue/{queuename}` format.
*   If you use an MNS topic as the notification method, specify the value in the `acs:mns:{region-id}:{account-id}:topic/{topicname}` format.
*   If you use an Operation Orchestration Service (OOS) template as the notification method, specify the value in the `acs:oos:{region-id}:{account-id}:template/{templatename}` format.

The variables in the preceding formats have the following meanings:

*   region-id: the region ID of the scaling group.
*   account-id: the ID of the Alibaba Cloud account.
*   queuename: the name of the MNS queue.
*   topicname: the name of the MNS topic.
*   templatename: the name of the OOS template.
The region ID of the scaling group.

The status that you want to specify for the lifecycle hook. Valid values: Valid values:

*   Active
*   InActive

If you do not specify this parameter, the status of the lifecycle hook remains unchanged after you call this operation.

>  By default, a new lifecycle hook is in the **Active** state.

- Specify both the scaling group ID (`ScalingGroupId`) and the lifecycle hook name (`LifecycleHookName`), because within a scaling group, each lifecycle hook name is unique.

*   region-id: the ID of the region where the scaling group resides.
*   account-id: the ID of the Alibaba Cloud account.
*   queuename: the name of the MNS queue.
*   topicname: the name of the MNS topic.

The type of notification N for scaling activities or resource changes. Valid values of N: 1 to 8. Specify multiple values in the repeated list form.

You can call the [DescribeNotificationTypes](~~71117~~) operation to query the value of this parameter.

items.description:

You can call the [DescribeNotificationTypes](~~71117~~) operation to query the value of this parameter.

schema.description: The ID of the region where the scaling group resides.

The time zone for message notifications.  
The offset of the time zone relative to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), such as UTC+8 (China Standard Time) or UTC-7 (Mountain Standard Time).

The codec of the notification message content. Valid values:

- PlainText: No encoding is applied. The message is transmitted in plaintext.
- Base64: The message is encoded in Base64.

Default value: Base64.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling configuration that you want to modify.

Specifies whether the instance is an I/O optimized instance. Valid values:

*   none: The instance is a non-I/O optimized instance.
*   optimized: The instance is an I/O optimized instance.

The preemption policy that you want to apply to pay-as-you-go instances and preemptible instances. Valid values:

*   NoSpot: The instance is created as a pay-as-you-go instance.
*   SpotWithPriceLimit: The instance is created as a preemptible instance with a user-defined maximum hourly price.
*   SpotAsPriceGo: The instance is a preemptible instance for which the market price at the time of purchase is used as the bid price.

The name of the scaling configuration. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). It must start with a letter or a digit.

The name of the scaling configuration must be unique within a scaling group in a region. If you do not specify this parameter, the value of the ScalingConfigurationId parameter is used.
The name of the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance that is created by Auto Scaling based on the scaling configuration.

The hostname of the ECS instance. The hostname cannot start or end with a period (.) or a hyphen (-). The hostname also cannot contain consecutive periods (.) or hyphens (-). Naming conventions:

*   Windows instances: The hostname must be 2 to 15 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, and hyphens (-). The hostname cannot contain periods (.) or contain only digits.
*   Other instances such as Linux instances: The hostname must be 2 to 64 characters in length. You can use periods (.) to separate a hostname into multiple segments. Each segment can contain letters, digits, and hyphens (-).

The ID of the image that is used by Auto Scaling to create instances.

>  If the image that is specified in the scaling configuration contains a system disk and data disks, the data that is stored in the data disks is cleared after you modify the image.

The name of the image. The name must be unique in a region. If you specify the ImageId parameter, the ImageName parameter is ignored.

You cannot use the ImageName parameter to specify images that are purchased from Alibaba Cloud Marketplace.

The number of vCPUs.

You can specify the number of vCPUs and the memory size to determine the range of instance types. For example, you can set Cpu to 2 and Memory to 16 to specify instance types that have 2 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory. If you specify the Cpu and Memory parameters, Auto Scaling determines the available instance types based on factors such as I/O optimization requirements and zones. Then, Auto Scaling preferentially creates instances of the instance type that is provided at the lowest price.

>  You can specify CPU and memory specifications to determine the range of instance types only if the Scaling Policy parameter is set to Cost Optimization Policy and no instance type is specified in the scaling configuration.

The memory size.

You can specify the number of vCPUs and the memory size to determine the range of instance types. For example, you can set Cpu to 2 and Memory to 16 to specify instance types that have 2 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory. If you specify the Cpu and Memory parameters, Auto Scaling determines the available instance types based on factors such as I/O optimization requirements and zones. Then, Auto Scaling preferentially creates instances of the instance type that is provided at the lowest price.

>  You can specify CPU and memory specifications to determine the range of instance types only if the Scaling Policy parameter is set to Cost Optimization Policy and no instance type is specified in the scaling configuration.

The billing method for network usage. Valid values:

*   PayByBandwidth: You are charged for the maximum available bandwidth that is specified by the InternetMaxBandwidthOut parameter.
*   PayByTraffic: You are charged for the actual traffic that is used. The InternetMaxBandwidthOut parameter specifies only the maximum available bandwidth.

The maximum outbound public bandwidth. Unit: Mbit/s.

*   If you set the InternetChargeType parameter to PayByBandwidth and you leave this parameter empty, this parameter is automatically set to 0.
*   If you set the InternetChargeType parameter to PayByTraffic and you leave this parameter empty, an error is reported.

The category of the system disk. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD
*   cloud_essd: enhanced SSD (ESSD)
*   ephemeral_ssd: local standard SSD
*   cloud_auto: ESSD AutoPL disk

You cannot specify the SystemDisk.Category and `SystemDiskCategories.N` parameters at the same time. If you do not specify the SystemDisk.Category or `SystemDiskCategories.N` parameters, the default value of the SystemDisk.Category parameter is used. The default value of this parameter for non-I/O optimized instances of Generation I instance types is cloud. The default value of this parameter for instances of other types is cloud_efficiency.

The size of the system disk. Unit: GiB.

*   Valid values if you set the SystemDisk.Category parameter to cloud: 20 to 500.
*   Valid values if you set the SystemDisk.Category parameter to cloud_efficiency: 20 to 500
*   Valid values if you set the SystemDisk.Category parameter to cloud_ssd: 20 to 500
*   Valid values if you set the SystemDisk.Category parameter to cloud_essd: 20 to 500
*   Valid values if you set the SystemDisk.Category parameter to cloud_essd: 20 to 500

The value of the SystemDisk.Size parameter must be greater than or equal to max{20, ImageSize}.

The name of the system disk. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (\_), and hyphens (-). The name must start with a letter but cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.
The description of the system disk. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length. The description can contain letters but cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.
The ID of the automatic snapshot policy that you want to apply to the system disk.

The performance level (PL) of the system disk of the ESSD category. Valid values:

*   PL0: An ESSD can deliver up to 10,000 random read/write IOPS.
*   PL1: An ESSD can deliver up to 50,000 random read/write IOPS.
*   PL2: An ESSD can deliver up to 100,000 random read/write IOPS.
*   PL3: An ESSD can deliver up to 1,000,000 random read/write IOPS.

>  For more information about how to select ESSD PLs, see [ESSDs](~~122389~~).
The weight of the ECS instance as a backend server. Valid values: 1 to 100.
The user data of the ECS instance. The data must be encoded in Base64. The maximum size of the data before encoding is 16 KB.

The name of the key pair that is used to log on to an ECS instance.

*   Windows instances do not use this parameter.
*   By default, the username and password authentication method is disabled for Linux instances.

The name of the RAM role that is associated with the ECS instance. The name is provided and maintained by Resource Access Management (RAM). You can call the [ListRoles](~~28713~~) operation to query the available RAM roles. For more information about how to create a RAM role, see [CreateRole](~~28710~~).
Specifies whether to use the password that is preconfigured in the image. Before you use this parameter, make sure that a password is configured for the image.

The tags of the ECS instance. The tags must be specified in the key-value format. You can specify up to 20 tags. The following rules apply to tag keys and tag values:

*   A tag key can be up to 64 characters in length. The key cannot start with `acs:` or `aliyun`, and cannot contain `http://` or `https://`. You cannot specify an empty string as a tag key.
*   A tag value can be up to 128 characters in length. The value cannot start with `acs:` or `aliyun`, and cannot contain `http://` or `https://`. You can specify an empty string as a tag value.
The ID of the deployment set to which the ECS instance belongs.
The ID of the security group with which the ECS instance is associated. ECS instances that are associated with the same security group can access each other.

Specifies whether to overwrite existing data. Valid values:

*   true
*   false
The ID of the resource group to which the ECS instance belongs.
The ID of the Elastic High Performance Computing (E-HPC) cluster to which the ECS instance belongs.
The description of the ECS instance. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length. The description can contain letters but cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.
The number of randomly generated IPv6 addresses that you want to allocate to the elastic network interface (ENI).

The performance mode of the burstable instance. Valid values:

*   Standard: standard mode. For more information, see the "Standard mode" section in the [Overview](~~59977~~) topic of burstable instances.
*   Unlimited: unlimited mode. For more information, see the "Unlimited mode" section in the [Overview](~~59977~~) topic of burstable instances.

The name of the image family. You can specify this parameter to obtain the latest custom images that are available in the specified image family. You can use the images to create instances. If you specify the ImageId parameter, you cannot specify the ImageFamily parameter.
The zone ID of the ECS instance.

The ID of the dedicated host on which you want to create the ECS instance. Preemptible instances cannot be created on dedicated hosts. If you specify the DedicatedHostId parameter, the SpotStrategy and SpotPriceLimit parameters are ignored.

You can call the [DescribeDedicatedHosts](~~134242~~) operation to query dedicated host IDs.

Specifies whether to associate an instance on a dedicated host with the dedicated host. Valid values:

*   default: does not associate the instance with the dedicated host. If you start an instance that was stopped in economical mode and the original dedicated host of the instance has insufficient resources, the instance is automatically deployed to another dedicated host in the automatic deployment resource pool.
*   host: associates the instance with the dedicated host. If you start an instance that was stopped in economical mode, the instance remains on the original dedicated host. If the original dedicated host has insufficient resources, the instance cannot be started.

Specifies whether to create the instance on a dedicated host. Valid values:

*   default: does not create the instance on a dedicated host.
*   host: creates the instance on a dedicated host. If you do not specify the DedicatedHostId parameter, the system selects a dedicated host for the instance.
The options of the scheduler.

The type of the private pool. A private pool is generated after an elasticity assurance or a capacity reservation takes effect. You can select the private pool when you start an instance. Valid values:

*   Open: open private pool. The system selects a matching open private pool to start the instance. If no matching open private pools are found, the resources in the public pool are used. In this case, you do not need to specify the PrivatePoolOptions.Id parameter.
*   Target: specified private pool. The resources in the specified private pool are used to start the instance. If the specified private pool is unavailable, the instance cannot be started. If you set this parameter to Target, you must specify the PrivatePoolOptions.Id parameter.
*   None: no private pool. The resources in private pools are not used to start the instance.
The ID of the private pool. The ID of a private pool is the same as the ID of the elasticity assurance or capacity reservation for which the private pool is generated.

The retention period of the preemptible instance. Unit: hours. Valid values: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6.

*   The following retention periods are available in invitational preview: 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 hours. If you want to set this parameter to one of these values, submit a ticket.
*   If you set this parameter to 0, no retention period is specified for the preemptible instance.
The interruption mode of the preemptible instance. Default value: Terminate. Set the value to Terminate, which specifies that the preemptible instance is to be released.
The data disks.

PerformanceLevel.description:
The PL of data disk N that is of the ESSD category. If you set the DataDisk.N.Category parameter to cloud_essd, the N value must be the same as the N value in DataDisk.N.Category. Valid values:

*   PL0: An ESSD can deliver up to 10,000 random read/write IOPS.
*   PL1: An ESSD can deliver up to 50,000 random read/write IOPS.

AutoSnapshotPolicyId.description: The ID of the automatic snapshot policy that you want to apply to data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16.

Encrypted.description:
Specifies whether to encrypt data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

Description.description: The description of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. The description must be 2 to 256 characters in length. The description can contain letters but cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.

SnapshotId.description:
The ID of the snapshot that you want to use to create data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. If you specify this parameter, the DataDisk.N.Size parameter is ignored. The size of the disk is the same as the size of the specified snapshot.

If you specify a snapshot created on or before July 15, 2013, the operation fails and the system returns InvalidSnapshot.TooOld.

Categories.description:
Category N of data disk N. The first N in DataDisk.N.Categories.N represents the serial number of the data disk. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. The second N in DataDisk.N.Categories.N represents the serial number of the category of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 4. You can specify up to four data disk categories in a scaling configuration. A smaller value of N specifies a higher priority. If Auto Scaling cannot create instances by using the disk that has the highest priority, Auto Scaling creates instances by using the disk that has the next highest priority. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk. The DeleteWithInstance attribute of a basic disk that is created together with the instance is set to true.
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk.
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD.
*   cloud_essd: ESSD.

>  You cannot specify the DataDisk.N.Categories.N and `DataDisk.N.Category` parameters at the same time.

items.description:
Category N of data disk N. The first N in DataDisk.N.Categories.N represents the serial number of the data disk. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. The second N in DataDisk.N.Categories.N represents the serial number of the category of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 4. You can specify up to four data disk categories in a scaling configuration. A smaller value of N specifies a higher priority. If Auto Scaling cannot create instances by using the disk that has the highest priority, Auto Scaling creates instances by using the disk that has the next highest priority. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk. The DeleteWithInstance attribute of a basic disk that is created together with the instance is set to true.
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk.
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD.
*   cloud_essd: ESSD.

>  You cannot specify the DataDisk.N.Categories.N and `DataDisk.N.Category` parameters at the same time.

Size.description:
The size of data disk N. Unit: GiB. Valid values of N: 1 to 16.

*   Valid values if you set the DataDisk.N.Category parameter to cloud: 5 to 2000.
*   Valid values if you set the DataDisk.N.Category parameter to cloud_efficiency: 20 to 32768.
*   Valid values if you set the DataDisk.N.Category parameter to cloud_essd: 20 to 32768.
*   Valid values if you set the DataDisk.N.Category parameter to ephemeral_ssd: 5 to 800.

The value of the DataDisk.N.Size parameter must be greater than or equal to the size of the snapshot that is specified by the SnapshotId parameter.

Device.description: The mount target of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. If you do not specify this parameter, the system automatically assigns a mount target when Auto Scaling creates ECS instances. The name of the mount target ranges from /dev/xvdb to /dev/xvdz.

DiskName.description: The name of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores (\_), and hyphens (-). The name must start with a letter but cannot start with `http://` or `https://`.

Category.description:
The category of data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk. The DeleteWithInstance attribute of a basic disk that is created together with the instance is set to true.
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk.
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD.
*   cloud_essd: ESSD.
*   ephemeral_ssd: local standard SSD.
*   cloud_auto: ESSD AutoPL disk.

You cannot specify the DataDisk.N.Category and `DataDisk.N.Categories.N` parameters at the same time. If you do not specify the DataDisk.N.Category or `DataDisk.N.Categories.N` parameters, the default value of the DataDisk.N.Category parameter is used.

*   The default value is cloud_efficiency for I/O optimized instances.
*   The default value is cloud for non-I/O optimized instances.

DeleteWithInstance.description:
Specifies whether to release data disk N when the instance to which data disk N is attached is released. Valid values of N: 1 to 16. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

This parameter is available only for independent disks whose DataDisk.N.Category parameter is set to cloud, cloud_efficiency, cloud_ssd, or cloud_essd. If you specify this parameter for disks of other categories, an error is reported.

KMSKeyId.description: The ID of the Key Management Service (KMS) key that is used to encrypt data disk N. Valid values of N: 1 to 16.

ProvisionedIops.description:
The preconfigured input/output operations per second (IOPS) for data disk N.

>  IOPS measures the number of read and write operations that an Elastic Block Storage (EBS) device can process per second.

BurstingEnabled.description:
Specifies whether to enable the burst feature for data disk N. Valid values:

*   true

*   false

    **

    **Note** This parameter is available only if you set the `DataDisk.Category` parameter to `cloud_auto`.

schema.description:
Instance type N. If you specify this parameter, the InstanceType parameter is ignored. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

The first instance type has the highest priority. The priority decreases based on the specified orders of the instance types. Auto Scaling creates instances based on the priorities of instance types. If Auto Scaling cannot create instances of the instance type that has the highest priority, Auto Scaling creates instances of the instance type that has the next highest priority.

items.description: Information about instance types.

InstanceType.description:
Instance type N that you want to use to override the instance type that is specified in the launch template. If you want to specify the weighted capacity of instance type N in the scaling configuration, you must specify the InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType parameter and the InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter at the same time.

The InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType parameter specifies instance type N, and the InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter specifies the weighted capacity of the specified instance type in the scaling configuration. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  You cannot specify the InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType and InstanceTypes parameters at the same time.

For information about valid values of InstanceType in InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType, see [Instance families](~~25378~~).

WeightedCapacity.description:
The weight of instance type N. If you want to specify the weighted capacity of instance type N in the scaling configuration, you must specify the InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType parameter and the InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter at the same time. The value of N in the two parameters must be the same.

The weight specifies the capacity of an instance of instance type N in the scaling group. A higher weight specifies that a smaller number of instances of the specified instance type are required to meet the expected capacity requirement.

Performance metrics, such as the number of vCPUs and the memory size of each instance type, may vary. You can specify different weights for different instance types based on your business requirements.

Example:

*   Current capacity: 0
*   Expected capacity: 6
*   Capacity of ecs.c5.xlarge: 4

To meet the expected capacity requirement, Auto Scaling must create two ecs.c5.xlarge instances.

>  The capacity of the scaling group cannot exceed the sum of the maximum number of instances that is specified by the MaxSize parameter and the maximum weight of the instance types.

Valid values of WeightedCapacity in the InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter: 1 to 500.

items.description: Information about instance types in Intelligent mode.

Cores.description:
The number of vCPUs that is provided for instance type N in intelligent configuration mode. This parameter is used to filter the available instance types that meet the specified criteria. For more information, see [Overview of instance families](~~25378~~). Valid values of N: 1 to 10

Take note of the following items:

*   The InstancePatternInfo.N parameter is available only for scaling groups that reside in virtual private clouds (VPCs).
*   You must specify the InstancePatternInfo.N, InstancePatternInfo.N.Cores, and InstancePatternInfo.N.Memory parameters at the same time.
*   If you specify an instance type by using the InstanceType or InstanceTypes.N parameter, Auto Scaling preferentially uses the instance type that is specified by the InstanceType or InstanceTypes.N parameter for scale-out activities. If the specified instance type does not have sufficient inventory, Auto Scaling creates instances of the instance type that is specified by the InstancePatternInfo.N parameter and provided at the lowest price.

InstanceFamilyLevel.description:
The instance family level in intelligent configuration mode. This parameter is used to filter available instance types that meet the specified criteria. Valid values:

*   EntryLevel: shared instance type. Instances of this level are cost-effective, but do not provide stable computing performance. Instances of this level are suitable for scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low. For more information, see [Shared instance families](~~108489~~).
*   EnterpriseLevel: Instances of this level provide stable performance and dedicated resources, and are suitable for business scenarios that require high stability. For more information, see [Overview of instance families](~~25378~~).
*   CreditEntryLevel: This value is available only for burstable instances. CPU credits are used to ensure computing performance. This level is suitable for scenarios in which the CPU utilization is low but may fluctuate in specific cases. For more information, see [Overview](~~59977~~) of burstable instances

Valid values of N: 1 to 10

MaxPrice.description:
The maximum hourly price for a pay-as-you-go instance or a preemptible instance in intelligent configuration mode. This parameter is used to filter the available instance types that meet the specified criteria. Valid values of N: 1 to 10

>  If you set the SpotStrategy parameter to SpotWithPriceLimit, you must specify this parameter. In other cases, you do not need to specify this parameter.

Memory.description: The memory size that is provided for instance type N in intelligent configuration mode. Unit: GiB. This parameter is used to filter the available instance types that meet the specified criteria. For more information, see [Overview of instance families](~~25378~~). Valid values of N: 1 to 10

Architecture.description:

*   Heterogeneous: heterogeneous architecture, such as GPUs and FPGAs.

*   Arm: ARM architecture.
*   SuperComputeCluster: Super Computing Cluster architecture.

By default, all values are included.

MinimumEniIpv6AddressQuantity.description: The minimum upper limit of IPv6 addresses per Elastic Network Interface (ENI) desired for the instance.

MinimumInitialCredit.description: The minimum initial CPU credits for burstable instances of types t5 and t6 desired for the instance.

MinimumBaselineCredit.description: The minimum baseline vCPU computing performance (sum of all vCPUs) expected for burstable instances of type t5 or t6.

MinimumMemorySize.description: The minimum memory size desired for the instance. Unit: GiB.

MaximumMemorySize.description: The maximum memory that the instance requires. Unit: GiB.

MinimumGpuAmount.description: The minimum number of GPUs desired for the instance. Valid values: positive integers greater than or equal to 1.

MaximumGpuAmount.description: The maximum number of GPUs desired for the instance. Valid values: positive integers greater than or equal to 1.

schema.description:
Category N of the system disk. Valid values of N: 1 to 4. A smaller value of N indicates a higher priority. If Auto Scaling cannot create instances by using the disk that has the highest priority, Auto Scaling creates instances by using the disk that has the next highest priority. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD
*   cloud_essd: ESSD

>  You cannot specify the SystemDiskCategories.N and `SystemDisk.Category` parameters at the same time.

items.description:
Category N of the system disk. Valid values of N: 1 to 4. A smaller value of N indicates a higher priority. If Auto Scaling cannot create instances by using the disk that has the highest priority, Auto Scaling creates instances by using the disk that has the next highest priority. Valid values:

*   cloud: basic disk
*   cloud_efficiency: ultra disk
*   cloud_ssd: standard SSD
*   cloud_essd: ESSD

>  You cannot specify the SystemDiskCategories.N and `SystemDisk.Category` parameters at the same time.

schema.description:
The password for the ECS instance. The password must be 8 to 30 characters in length and include at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Supported special characters are:

`()~!@#$%^&*-_+=\|{}[]:;'<>,.?/

For Windows instances, the password cannot start with a forward slash (/).

> If you include the Password parameter, we recommend that you send your request over HTTPS to prevent password leakage.

Specifies whether to encrypt the system disk. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

Default value: false.
The ID of the KMS key that is used to encrypt the system disk.

The encryption algorithm that is used to encrypt the system disk. Valid values:

*   AES-256
*   SM4-128

Default value: AES-256.

The preconfigured IOPS for the system disk.

>  IOPS measures the number of read and write operations that an EBS device can process per second.

Specifies whether to enable the burst feature for the system disk. Valid values:

*   true

*   false

    **

    **Note** This parameter is available only if you set the `SystemDisk.Category` parameter to `cloud_auto`.

For more information about whether an ECS instance uses the ecs-user user user to log on to an ECS instance, see Manage the login name of an ECS instance. Value range:

- true: Yes.
- false: No.

Default value: false.

The ECS instance release protection property. This property applies only to pay-as-you-go instances and indicates whether the instance can be directly released through the ECS console or the API (DeleteInstance). Valid values:
- true: Enables instance release protection, which means the instance cannot be directly released through the ECS console or the API (preventing accidental deletion of instances scaled out by automatic scaling).
- false: Disables instance release protection, which means the instance can be directly released through the ECS console or the API.

> This property does not affect normal scale-in activities of automatic scaling. When a scale-in activity occurs, pay-as-you-go instances with release protection enabled can still be released normally.
Storage set ID.
The maximum number of partitions in a storage set. Valid values: integers greater than or equal to 2.

Custom priority for the **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination.

> This parameter is valid only when the scaling group's ``scaling policy`` is set to `Priority Policy`.

If an ECS instance cannot be created using a **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination with a higher priority, the automatic scaling service automatically selects the next-priority **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination to create the ECS instance.

> If custom priorities are specified only for some **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combinations, the unspecified combinations have lower priority than the specified ones. The priority of unspecified combinations is then determined sequentially based on the order of virtual switches in the scaling group and the order of instance types in the scaling configuration. For example, if the virtual switches in the scaling group are ordered as vsw1, vsw2, and the instance types in the scaling configuration are ordered as type1, type2, and the custom priority order for the combinations is `["vsw2+type2", "vsw1+type2"]`, the final priority order becomes `vsw2+type2` > `vsw1+type2` > `vsw1+type1` > `vsw2+type1`.

items.description:
Custom priority for the **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination.

><notice>This parameter is valid only when the scaling group's ``scaling policy`` is set to `Priority Policy`.

InstanceType.description:
The `CustomPriorities` field specifies the custom priority for the **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination. The `CustomPriorities.N.InstanceType` parameter specifies the instance type of the ECS instance within the custom priority.

> This parameter is valid only when the scaling group's ``scaling policy`` is set to `Priority Policy`, and the specified instance type must be included in the instance type list of the scaling configuration.

If an ECS instance cannot be created using a **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination with a higher priority, the automatic scaling service automatically selects the next-priority **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combination to create the ECS instance.

> If custom priorities are specified only for some **ECS instance type + virtual switch** combinations, the unspecified combinations have lower priority than the specified ones. The priority of unspecified combinations is then determined sequentially based on the order of virtual switches in the scaling group and the order of instance types in the scaling configuration. For example, if the virtual switches in the scaling group are ordered as vsw1, vsw2, and the instance types in the scaling configuration are ordered as type1, type2, and the custom priority order for the combinations is `["vsw2+type2", "vsw1+type2"]`, the final priority order becomes `vsw2+type2` > `vsw1+type2` > `vsw1+type1` > `vsw2+type1`.

VswitchId.description:
The `CustomPriorities.N.VswitchId` parameter specifies the ID of the virtual switch in the custom priority.

> This parameter is valid only when the scaling group's ``scaling policy`` is set to `Priority Policy`, and the specified vSwitch must be included in the vSwitch list of the scaling group.

schema.description: The list of Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs).

items.description: The list of Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs).

InstanceType.description:
The type of Elastic Network Interface (ENI). When this parameter is used, you must configure the primary ENI by using `NetworkInterfaces.N`. In this case, you cannot simultaneously specify the `SecurityGroupId` or `SecurityGroupIds.N` parameters. Valid values:

- Primary: Primary ENI.
- Secondary: Secondary ENI.

Default Value: Secondary.

NetworkInterfaceTrafficMode.description:
The communication mode of the network interface card. Valid values:

- Standard: Uses the TCP communication mode.
- HighPerformance: Enables the Elastic RDMA Interface (ERI) and uses the RDMA communication mode.

Default Value: Standard.  
> The number of Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) in RDMA mode cannot exceed the limit of the instance family. For more information, see [Instance Families](~~25378~~).

Ipv6AddressCount.description:
The number of randomly generated IPv6 addresses to assign to the primary ENI. Note the following:

- This parameter takes effect only when `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Primary`.
- You cannot set this parameter if `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Secondary` or is empty.
- After you set this parameter, you cannot set the `Ipv6AddressCount` parameter again.

SecurityGroupIds.description: The ID or IDs of one or more security groups to which the ENI belongs.

items.description:
The ID or IDs of one or more security groups to which the ENI belongs. Note the following:

- If `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Primary`, you must specify this parameter. In this case, it functions the same as `SecurityGroupIds.N`, but you cannot simultaneously specify `SecurityGroupId` or `SecurityGroupIds.N`.
- If `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Secondary` or is empty, this parameter is optional. The default value is the security group of the ECS instance (that is, the security group of the primary ENI).

SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount.description:
The number of secondary private IPv4 addresses to assign to the network interface card. Valid values: 1 to 49.

- The value must not exceed the IP address quantity limit for the instance type. For more information, see [instance family](~~25378~~).
- When you set NetworkInterface.N.SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount, the system assigns the specified number of secondary private IPv4 addresses (excluding the primary private IP of the network interface card) randomly from the available segment of the virtual switch (NetworkInterface.N.VSwitchId) to which the network interface card belongs.

schema.description: The ID of the dedicated host cluster.
Security options.

ConfidentialComputingMode.description:
The confidential computing mode. Valid values:
- Enclave: The ECS instance uses an enclave to build a confidential computing environment. For more information, see [Build a confidential computing environment by using enclaves](~~203433~~).
- TDX: A TDX confidential computing environment is built. For more information, see [Build a TDX confidential computing environment](~~479090~~).

schema.description:
Whether to enable the access channel for instance metadata. Valid values:

- enabled: Enable.
- disabled: Disable.

Default value: enabled.

> For more information about instance metadata, see [Overview of instance metadata](~~108460~~).

Whether to enforce the use of hardened mode (IMDSv2) when accessing instance metadata. Valid values:

- optional: Hardened mode is not enforced.
- required: Hardened mode is enforced. After this value is set, instance metadata cannot be accessed in NAT mode.

Default Value: optional.

> For more information about access modes for instance metadata, see [Instance metadata access mode](~~108460~~).

The maximum inbound public bandwidth, measured in Mbit/s. Valid values:

- If the purchased outbound public bandwidth is less than or equal to 10 Mbit/s: 1 to 10, with a default value of 10.
- If the purchased outbound public bandwidth is greater than 10 Mbit/s: 1 to the value of `InternetMaxBandwidthOut`, with a default value equal to the value of `InternetMaxBandwidthOut`.

The resource pool policy used when creating an instance. After you set this parameter, note the following:

- This parameter takes effect only when creating pay-as-you-go instances.

- This parameter cannot be specified together with PrivatePoolOptions.MatchCriteria or PrivatePoolOptions.Id.

Strategy.description:
The resource pool includes private pools generated after Elasticity Assurance or Capacity Reservation services take effect, as well as public pools, which are available for instance startup. Valid values:

- PrivatePoolFirst: Prefer private pools. When this strategy is selected and ResourcePoolOptions.PrivatePoolIds is specified, the specified private pools are used first. If no private pool is specified or the specified private pool lacks sufficient capacity, an open-type private pool is automatically matched. If no eligible private pool exists, the instance is created in a public pool.

- PrivatePoolOnly: Use only private pools. When this strategy is selected, you must specify ResourcePoolOptions.PrivatePoolIds. If the specified private pools lack sufficient capacity, instance startup fails.

- None: Do not use any resource pool policy.

Default value: None.

PrivatePoolIds.description: The private pool ID, which corresponds to either an Elasticity Assurance service ID or a Capacity Reservation service ID. This parameter accepts only Target-mode private pool IDs.

items.description: The private pool ID, which corresponds to either an Elasticity Assurance service ID or a Capacity Reservation service ID. This parameter accepts only Target-mode private pool IDs. The value range for N is 1 to 20.

ModifyScalingConfiguration.title: Modify a scaling configuration
ModifyScalingConfiguration.description:
## API Guide

- If you modify the name of a scaling configuration, ensure that no other scaling configuration in the same scaling group has the same name.
- You can attach the primary network interface card (NIC) by using either of the following methods. However, note that only one method can be used per API call to configure the primary NIC. Using both methods simultaneously will cause the API call to fail and return an error message:
    - Directly configure the primary NIC by using parameters such as `SecurityGroupId`, `SecurityGroupIds.N`, and `Ipv6AddressCount`.
    - Configure both the primary and secondary NICs by using the `NetworkInterfaces.N` parameter. When this parameter is used, the primary NIC configuration must be specified. Specifically:
        - If `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Primary`, it indicates the primary NIC.
        - If `NetworkInterfaces.N.InstanceType` is set to `Secondary` or left empty, it indicates a secondary ENI.

    > When modifying a scaling configuration, if you choose one of the above methods to update the NIC configuration, the NIC configuration previously set by the other method will be deleted.

schema.description: The ID of the scaling group that you want to modify.

The name of the scaling group. The name of each scaling group must be unique in a region. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The name must start with a letter or a digit.

The minimum number of ECS instances in the scaling group. When the number of ECS instances in the scaling group is less than the value of the MinSize parameter, Auto Scaling automatically adds ECS instances until the number of instances is equal to the value of the `MinSize` parameter.

>  The value of the `MinSize` parameter must be less than or equal to the value of the `MaxSize` parameter.

The maximum number of ECS instances in the scaling group. When the number of ECS instances in the scaling group is greater than the value of the MaxSize parameter, Auto Scaling automatically removes ECS instances from the scaling group until the number of instances is equal to the value of the `MaxSize` parameter.

The value range of the MaxSize parameter varies based on the instance quota. You can go to [Quota Center](https://quotas.console.aliyun.com/products/ess/quotas) to check the quota of instances that can be added to a scaling group.****

For example, if the quota of instances that can be added to a scaling group is 2,000, the valid values of the `MaxSize` parameter range from 0 to 2000.

The cooldown time of the scaling group after a scaling activity is triggered. Valid values: 0 to 86400. Unit: seconds.

During the cooldown time, Auto Scaling executes only scaling activities that are triggered by event-triggered tasks monitored by CloudMonitor.

The first step to remove ECS instances from the scaling group. Valid values:

*   OldestInstance: removes ECS instances that are added at the earliest point in time to the scaling group.
*   NewestInstance: removes ECS instances that are most recently added to the scaling group.
*   OldestScalingConfiguration: removes ECS instances that are created based on the earliest scaling configuration.
*   CustomPolicy: removes ECS instances based on the custom scale-in policy (Function).

>  The scaling configuration source specified by OldestScalingConfiguration can be a scaling configuration or a launch template. The CustomPolicy setting is available only for the RemovalPolicy.1 parameter. If you set the RemovalPolicy.1 parameter to CustomPolicy, you must also specify the CustomPolicyARN parameter.

The second step to remove ECS instances from the scaling group. Valid values:

*   OldestInstance: removes ECS instances that are added at the earliest point in time to the scaling group.

*   NewestInstance: removes ECS instances that are most recently added to the scaling group.

*   OldestScalingConfiguration: removes ECS instances that are created based on the earliest scaling configuration.

    **

    **Note** The scaling configuration source specified by OldestScalingConfiguration can be a scaling configuration or a launch template.

The third step to remove ECS instances from the scaling group. Valid values:

*   OldestInstance: removes ECS instances that are added at the earliest point in time to the scaling group.
*   NewestInstance: removes ECS instances that are most recently added to the scaling group.
*   OldestScalingConfiguration: removes ECS instances that are created based on the earliest scaling configuration.

>  The scaling configuration source specified by OldestScalingConfiguration can be a scaling configuration or a launch template.
The ID of the active scaling configuration in the scaling group.

The health check mode of the scaling group. Valid values:

*   NONE: Auto Scaling does not perform health checks on instances in the scaling group.
*   ECS: Auto Scaling performs health checks on ECS instances in the scaling group.
The ID of the launch template that is used by Auto Scaling to create instances.

The version number of the launch template. Valid values:

*   A fixed template version number.
*   Default: the default template version.
*   Latest: the latest template version.

The minimum number of pay-as-you-go instances required in the scaling group. Valid values: 0 to 1000. If the number of pay-as-you-go instances is less than the value of this parameter, Auto Scaling preferentially creates pay-as-you-go instances.

If the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to `COMPOSABLE` Policy, the default value is 0.

The percentage of pay-as-you-go instances among the excess instances when the requirement on the minimum number of pay-as-you-go instances is met. Valid values: 0 to 100.

If the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to `COMPOSABLE` Policy, the default value is 100.

Specifies whether to supplement preemptible instances. If you set this parameter to true, Auto Scaling creates an instance to replace a preemptible instance when Auto Scaling receives a system message that indicates the preemptible instance is to be reclaimed.

Specifies whether to automatically create pay-as-you-go instances to meet the requirement on the number of ECS instances in the scaling group when the number of preemptible instances cannot be reached due to reasons such as costs and insufficient resources. This parameter takes effect only if you set the MultiAZPolicy parameter in the CreateScalingGroup operation to COST_OPTIMIZED. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

The number of instance types that you specify. Auto Scaling creates preemptible instances of multiple instance types that are provided at the lowest price. Valid values: 0 to 10.

If the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to `COMPOSABLE` Policy, the default value is 2.

The expected number of ECS instances in the scaling group. Auto Scaling automatically maintains the expected number of ECS instances that you specify. The expected number cannot be greater than the value of the MaxSize parameter and cannot be less than the value of the MinSize parameter.

Specifies whether to enable deletion protection for the scaling group. Valid values:

*   true: enables deletion protection for the scaling group. This way, the scaling group cannot be deleted.
*   false: disables deletion protection for the scaling group.

The scaling policy for the multi-zone scaling group that contains ECS instances. Valid values:

*   PRIORITY: The first vSwitch specified by using the VSwitchIds.N parameter has the highest priority. Auto Scaling scales instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the highest priority resides. If the scaling fails, Auto Scaling scales instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the next highest priority resides.

*   COST_OPTIMIZED: Auto Scaling creates ECS instances whose vCPUs are provided at the lowest price during scale-out activities and removes ECS instances whose vCPUs are provided at the highest price during scale-in activities. If preemptible instance types are specified in the active scaling configuration, Auto Scaling preferentially creates preemptible instances. You can use the `CompensateWithOnDemand` parameter to specify whether to automatically create pay-as-you-go instances when Auto Scaling fails to create preemptible instances.

    **

    **Note** The COST_OPTIMIZED setting takes effect only when you specify multiple instance types or when you specify at least one preemptible instance type.

*   BALANCE: Auto Scaling evenly distributes ECS instances across zones that are specified for the scaling group. If ECS instances are unevenly distributed across zones due to insufficient resources, you can call the [RebalanceInstance](~~71516~~) operation to evenly distribute the instances across the zones.

*   COMPOSABLE: You can flexibly combine the preceding policies based on your business requirements.

The IDs of vSwitches.

This parameter takes effect only when the network type of the scaling group is VPC. The specified vSwitches and the scaling group must reside in the same VPC.

The vSwitches can reside in different zones. The vSwitches are sorted in ascending order. The first vSwitch specified by using the VSwitchIds parameter has the highest priority. If Auto Scaling fails to create ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the highest priority resides, Auto Scaling creates ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the next highest priority resides.

items.description:
The ID of vSwitch N. Valid values of N: 1 to 5.

This parameter is available only if the network type of the scaling group is virtual private cloud (VPC). The specified vSwitches and the scaling group must reside in the same VPC.

The vSwitches can reside in different zones. The vSwitches are sorted in ascending order based on the value of N. 1 specifies the highest priority. A greater value of N specifies a lower priority. If Auto Scaling fails to create ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the highest priority resides, Auto Scaling creates ECS instances in the zone where the vSwitch that has the next highest priority resides.

schema.description: Details of the instance types that are specified in the extended configurations of the launch template.

items.description: Launch template information.

InstanceType.description:
Instance type N. The instance type that is specified by using this parameter overrides the instance type that is specified in the launch template. If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of instances, you must specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType and LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameters at the same time.

You can specify N instance types by using the Extended Configurations feature of the launch template. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  This parameter is available only if you specify the LaunchTemplateId parameter.

For information about the valid values of InstanceType in InstanceTypeOverride.N.InstanceType, see [Overview of instance families](~~25378~~).

WeightedCapacity.description:
The weight of instance type N. The weight of an instance type specifies the capacity of a single instance of the instance type in the scaling group. If you want to scale instances in the scaling group based on the weighted capacity of instances, you must specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter after you specify the LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType parameter. The values of N in the two parameters must be the same.

A higher weight specifies that a smaller number of instances of the specified instance type are required to meet the expected capacity requirement.

Performance metrics, such as the number of vCPUs and the memory size of each instance type, may vary. You can specify different weights for different instance types based on your business requirements.

Example:

*   Current capacity: 0
*   Expected capacity: 6
*   Capacity of ecs.c5.xlarge: 4

To meet the expected capacity requirement, Auto Scaling must create two ecs.c5.xlarge instances.

>  The capacity of the scaling group cannot exceed the sum of the maximum number of instances that is specified by the MaxSize parameter and the maximum weight of the instance type.

Valid values of WeightedCapacity in the InstanceTypeOverride.N.WeightedCapacity parameter: 1 to 500.

SpotPriceLimit.description:
The maximum bid price of instance type N that is specified by the `LaunchTemplateOverride.N.InstanceType` parameter. You can specify N instance types by using the Extended Configurations feature of the launch template. Valid values of N: 1 to 10.

>  This parameter is available only if you specify the `LaunchTemplateId` parameter.

schema.description:
Specifies whether to evenly distribute instances in the scaling group across multiple zones. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   true
*   false

Default value: false.

The allocation policy of instances. Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the allocation policy to create instances. The policy can be applied to pay-as-you-go instances and preemptible instances. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified orders of the instance types to create instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPU to create instances.

Default value: priority.

The allocation policy of preemptible instances. You can use this parameter to individually specify the allocation policy of preemptible instances. This parameter is available only if you set the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter to `COMPOSABLE`. Valid values:

*   priority: Auto Scaling selects instance types based on the specified orders of the instance types to create preemptible instances.
*   lowestPrice: Auto Scaling selects instance types that have the lowest unit price of vCPU to create preemptible instances.

Default value: priority.

The maximum life span of the instance in the scaling group. Unit: seconds.

Valid values: 86400 to `Integer.maxValue`. You can also set this parameter to 0. If you set this parameter to 0, the instance has an unlimited life span.

Default value: null.

>  You cannot specify this parameter for scaling groups that contain elastic container instances or scaling groups whose ScalingPolicy is set to recycle.
The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the custom scale-in policy (Function). This parameter is available only if you specify CustomPolicy as the first step of the instance removal policy.

Specifies whether the scaling group disables the expected number of instances feature. Valid values:  
- false: Enables the expected number of instances feature.  
- true: Disables the expected number of instances feature.  
> You can set this parameter to true (that is, disable the expected number of instances feature) only when the scaling group has no ongoing scaling activity. When this parameter is set to true, the current `DesiredCapacity` property of the scaling group is cleared, but the current number of instances in the scaling group remains unchanged.

Specifies the reclaim mode of the scaling group. Valid values:

- recycle: The scaling group uses the stop-and-reclaim mode.

- release: The scaling group uses the release mode.

- forcerelease: The scaling group uses the force-release mode.

    > If you select `forcerelease`, the system forcibly releases `running` instances during scale-down activities. Force-releasing an instance is equivalent to power-off, which erases all temporary data in the instance's memory and storage. The data cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when selecting this option.

- forcerecycle: The scaling group uses the force-stop-and-reclaim mode.

    > If you select `forcerecycle`, the system forcibly stops `running` instances during scale-down activities. Force-stopping an instance is equivalent to power-off, which erases all temporary data in the instance's memory and storage. The data cannot be recovered. Exercise caution when selecting this option.

The ScalingPolicy parameter specifies the reclaim mode of the scaling group. However, the specific action taken when an instance is removed from the scaling group is determined by the RemovePolicy parameter of the RemoveInstances operation. For more information, see [RemoveInstances](~~25955~~).

The health check method for the scaling group.

> You can specify multiple values for this parameter to enable multiple health check options. If the `HealthCheckType` parameter is set, this parameter is ignored.

items.description:
The list of health check methods for the scaling group. Valid values:

- NONE: No health check is performed.
- ECS: Performs health checks on instances in the scaling group (this value enables instance health checks for both ECS and ECI scaling groups).
- LOAD_BALANCER: Determines the health status of instances based on the health check results from the load balancer (CLB-type load balancing is not currently supported).

Default Value: ECS.

schema.description:
The timeout period, in seconds, to wait for an ECS instance to stop successfully during a scale-in process.

Valid values: 30 to 240.

> - This parameter takes effect only during scale-in operations when ScalingPolicy is set to release mode.  
- If this parameter is set, the system waits up to the specified StopInstanceTimeout duration for the instance to stop successfully. If the timeout is reached, the scale-in process continues regardless of whether the instance has stopped successfully.  
- If this parameter is not set, the system waits indefinitely until the instance stops successfully before proceeding with the scale-in. If stopping the instance fails, the scale-in process rolls back and the scale-in operation fails.  
- Setting this parameter to 0 cancels the current configuration of this parameter.
Capacity options.

OnDemandBaseCapacity.description:
The minimum number of on-demand instances required in an existing scaling group. If the number of on-demand instances in the scaling group is less than this value, the system prioritizes creating on-demand instances. Valid values: 0 to 1000.  

When the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to the `COMPOSABLE` policy, the default value is 0.

OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity.description:
The percentage of on-demand instances among the instances that exceed the minimum number specified by `OnDemandBaseCapacity`. Valid values: 0 to 100.  

When the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter is set to the `COMPOSABLE` policy, the default value is 100.

CompensateWithOnDemand.description:
When the `MultiAZPolicy` parameter of the `CreateScalingGroup` API is set to `COST_OPTIMIZED`, specifies whether the system is allowed to automatically attempt to create on-demand instances to meet the required number of ECS instances if it cannot create enough spot instances due to price or inventory constraints. Valid values:  

- true: Allowed.  
- false: Not allowed.

SpotAutoReplaceOnDemand.description:
When `CompensateWithOnDemand` is enabled, if the proportion of on-demand instances exceeds the `OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity` threshold, the system attempts to replace excess on-demand capacity with spot instances. This scenario commonly occurs when `CompensateWithOnDemand` causes a downgrade from spot instances to on-demand instances due to spot inventory or pricing issues. To avoid prolonged presence of on-demand instances, the system attempts to replace the excess on-demand capacity with spot instances. Valid values:  

- true: Allowed.  
- false: Not allowed.  

Default value: false.

PriceComparisonMode.description:
The price comparison mode for the scaling group's cost optimization policy. Valid values:  

- PricePerUnit: Compares prices based on the price per unit of capacity.  

  The capacity of an instance in the scaling group equals the weight assigned to its instance type, which defaults to 1 (that is, one ECS instance occupies one unit of capacity).  

- PricePerVCpu: Compares prices based on the price per vCPU.  

Default value: PricePerUnit.

schema.description:

If resource creation fails in a zone, the system degrades to another zone to ensure best-effort resource delivery.

- BalancedOnly:
If resource creation fails in a zone, the system does not degrade to another zone. The scale-out activity partially succeeds to prevent excessive imbalance of resources across zones.

ModifyScalingGroup.title: Modify a scaling group
ModifyScalingGroup.description:
## API Guide

- The following parameters cannot be modified:

    - RegionId

    - LoadBalancerId

        > To modify an SLB instance, use the [AttachLoadBalancers](~~85125~~) and [DetachLoadBalancers](~~85141~~) APIs.

    - DBInstanceId

        > To modify an RDS instance, use the [AttachDBInstances](~~85379~~) and [DetachDBInstances](~~85380~~) APIs.

- You can invoke this API only when the scaling group status is Active or Inactive.

- Enabling a new scaling configuration does not affect ECS instances or ECI instances that were created by earlier scaling configurations and are currently running.

- If you modify MaxSize and the current number of ECS or ECI instances in the scaling group exceeds MaxSize, the scaling group automatically removes ECS or ECI instances until the instance count equals MaxSize.

- If you modify MinSize and the current number of ECS or ECI instances in the scaling group falls below MinSize, the scaling group automatically adds ECS or ECI instances until the instance count equals MinSize.

- If DesiredCapacity is set for the scaling group and you modify DesiredCapacity such that it no longer matches the current number of ECS or ECI instances, the scaling group automatically adds or removes ECS or ECI instances until the instance count equals DesiredCapacity.

RebalanceInstances.title: Rebalance ECS Instance Distribution
RebalanceInstances.description:
## API Guide

Rebalancing distributes ECS instances by creating new ECS instances to replace existing ones in order to balance instance distribution across zones. New ECS instances are started before the existing ones are stopped. Rebalancing does not affect your application's performance or availability.

- This operation supports only multi-zone scaling groups where `MultiAZPolicy` is set to `BALANCE`, which ensures balanced distribution of ECS instances across multiple zones.

- You can perform a rebalancing operation only when the instance distribution within the scaling group is critically unbalanced. A single rebalancing activity can replace up to 20 ECS instances.

- During a rebalancing activity, if the number of instances in the scaling group is close to or has reached the specified maximum number of ECS instances (`MaxSize`) but further balancing is required, automatic scaling temporarily allows the instance count to exceed `MaxSize` by up to 10%. This temporary excess lasts until the instance distribution is balanced, typically between 1 and 6 minutes.

    > If 10% of the scaling group's maximum instance count is not an integer, the fractional part is rounded up, allowing an additional instance. For example, if the maximum instance count is 15, 10% equals 1.5 instances; thus, up to 2 extra instances are temporarily allowed.

RemoveInstances.title: Remove one or more ECS instances from a scaling group
RemoveInstances.summary: Remove one or more ECS instances from a scaling group.
RemoveInstances.description:
## API Guide

- Before invoking this API, ensure that the following conditions are met:

    - The scaling group is in the Enabled (Active) state.

    - There are no scaling activities currently executing in the scaling group.

When no scaling activity is in progress, this API can bypass the cooldown time (DefaultCooldown) and execute immediately.

- If an ECS instance was automatically created by automatic scaling, or was manually added but has been托管 to the scaling group, deleting it from the scaling group triggers the cost-saving hibernation effect or releases the instance.

- If an ECS instance was manually added and has not been托管 to the scaling group, deleting it from the scaling group does not stop or release the instance.

- If subtracting the number of instances specified in this request from the current total instance count (TotalCapacity) of the scaling group results in a value less than the minimum instance count (MinSize) configured for the scaling group, the API call fails.

A successful response from this API indicates only that the automatic scaling service has accepted the request and the scaling activity can be executed. It does not guarantee that the scaling activity will succeed. You must use the returned `ScalingActivityId` to check the execution status of the scaling activity.

ScaleWithAdjustment.title: Trigger Elastic Scaling Based on a Specified Adjustment Rule
ScaleWithAdjustment.description:
## API Guide

- Before invoking this API, ensure that the following conditions are met:
    - The scaling group is in the Active status.
    - There is no scaling activity currently executing in the scaling group.

- When no scaling activity is in progress within the scaling group, this API can bypass the cooldown time and directly execute a scaling activity.
- If the number of ECS instances to be added by the scaling rule plus the current total capacity of the scaling group exceeds the maximum instance count (MaxSize), the scaling activity is executed with Total Capacity set to MaxSize.
- If the current total capacity of the scaling group minus the number of ECS instances to be removed by the scaling rule falls below the minimum instance count (MinSize), the scaling activity is executed with Total Capacity set to MinSize.

A successful response from this API only indicates that the automatic scaling service has accepted the request and can proceed with the scaling activity. It does not guarantee that the scaling activity will succeed. You must use the returned `ScalingActivityId` to check the execution status of the scaling activity.

## API Guide

After an ECS instance is enabled with protection status:

- The instance remains in this state until you disable the protection.

- Even if changes in the number of instances in the scaling group or monitoring jobs trigger automatic scale-in activities, protected ECS instances will not be removed. StartInstanceRefresh.summary: You can invoke this API to refresh instances in a scaling group when you need to apply a new scaling configuration to the instances in the scaling group or update the image of the instances in the scaling group.
StartInstanceRefresh.description:
## API Guide
- Only one running instance refresh job is allowed per scaling group at any given time.
- This feature currently supports only ECS scaling groups that use the **priority policy** for scale-out. Scaling groups that **calculate scaling group capacity based on the number of vCPUs**, or use the **stop and revoke mode** or **force stop and revoke mode** for instance revocation, do not support this feature.
- Normal scale-in and scale-out operations can proceed during an instance refresh. However, any scale-out operation performed during the refresh uses the desired configuration specified in the instance refresh.
- Instances manually added to the scaling group, or those in the standby state or protection status, are ignored by the instance refresh job and will not be refreshed.

TagResources.description:
## API Guide

- A scaling group supports up to 20 attached tags.  
    > Before attaching tags, Alibaba Cloud validates the number of existing tags on the resource. If the limit is exceeded, an error message is returned.

- When the `Tag.N.Propagate` parameter is set to `true`, tags configured on the scaling group are synchronized only to instances that will be newly created in the scaling group, and not to instances already running in the scaling group.

- If a scaling configuration has tags defined and tag propagation from the scaling group is enabled, the tags on newly created instances are expected as follows:  
    - Include all tags from both the scaling configuration and the propagated tags from the scaling group.  
    - If a tag key in the scaling configuration matches a propagated tag key from the scaling group, the tag from the scaling configuration overwrites the propagated tag from the scaling group.
